title: Specify needs
description: This phase is triggered when a need for new statistics is identified, perhaps resulting from user feedback, or a review is undertaken. It includes all activities associated with engaging stakeholders to identify their detailed statistical needs (current or future), proposing high level solution options, and preparing a business case. In the modernized statistical environment, these activities are increasingly supported by automated and AI-powered processes—ranging from the synthesis and structuring of stakeholder inputs, through the analysis of options, to the automated drafting of business case materials. Routine and repetitive aspects of needs identification, consultation, and documentation are minimized for manual intervention, enabling staff to focus on higher-value tasks: interpreting context, establishing priorities, and making strategic decisions that cannot be automated. The phase thus leverages end-to-end process automation and AI wherever possible, supporting greater efficiency, responsiveness, and quality at the earliest stage of the statistical business process. The Specify Needs phase is broken down into six sub-processes (Figure 7), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because it centers on identifying new statistical needs, engaging stakeholders, assessing current and future requirements, analyzing options, and preparing business-case style materials. That requires capability in stakeholder consultation, requirements gathering, research and synthesis, and analysis of feasibility or impacts. The Junior Evaluation Officer directly fills this need because the role "provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data," "attends departmental and inter-departmental meetings... to discuss files / issues and evaluation requirements," and has communication skills to "discuss data requirements with Statistics Canada clients and evaluation colleagues" and to participate in "interviews, and focus groups." The role also supports option and business-case style analysis through "socio-economic analyses and cost-benefit analysis of programs" and by providing supporting data for "reports, presentations, briefing notes and memoranda for senior management."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because specifying needs requires translating stakeholder and program requirements into structured specifications and understanding what metadata will be needed to support a new or modified statistical program. That requires liaison with clients, interpretation of requirements, and analysis of options and impacts. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management in order to develop and translate requirements into specifications" and "interprets client requirements in order to determine options for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata." The role also "analyzes current production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation methods, procedures and systems in order to propose enhancements or alternatives," which aligns with proposing high-level solution options during needs specification.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because identifying needs for new statistics depends on gathering information from stakeholders, understanding data requirements, and translating subject-matter needs into specifications for future development. That requires data-oriented consultation, requirements elicitation, and analytical support. The Junior Data Analyst fills this need because the role "attends Departmental meetings, and interdepartmental and stakeholder meetings (as required), to gather data/information," "discusses data requirements with operations managers... other subject matter and systems specialists, clients or service providers to comprehend and elaborate the conditions within which statistical development and operations will occur," and "liaise[s] with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development." The role’s knowledge of the data science life cycle and research methods also supports analysis of possible solution approaches.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because specifying needs includes understanding operational implications of new statistical requirements and consulting with stakeholders on the conditions under which future collection and processing would occur. That requires operational requirements analysis, stakeholder engagement, and articulation of options and requirements. The Operations Officer fills this need because the role "meets with subject matter and systems specialists, clients, service providers and others, in order to comprehend and elaborate on the conditions within which statistical operations will occur," and "prepares reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems." The role also "assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems," which is directly relevant to high-level solution optioning in the needs phase.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because it requires identifying subject-matter needs, engaging users, assessing feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs, and translating needs into plans or specifications. That requires subject-matter analysis, liaison with users, and feasibility assessment. Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role "liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development, to suggest improvements to ongoing programs, to negotiate procedural modifications and to establish project plans, priorities and target dates." The role also has "knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to conduct studies and to develop/assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs," which directly supports the Specify Needs phase.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because specifying needs involves understanding user information needs, consulting with users, and considering the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs and outputs. That requires interpretation of user requests, consultative service, and feasibility analysis. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "provides statistical data and consultative services to users," "interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations," and "liaises with other specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development and to suggest improvements to ongoing programs." The role also has knowledge "to prepare information for studies and to review the feasibility and potential impact of new or modified statistical programs," which aligns directly with identifying needs and proposing solution options.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Identify needs
description: This sub-process includes the initial investigation and identification of what statistics are needed and what is needed of the statistics. In the modern process, AI and automated tools are used to continuously scan for new information requests from users, detect relevant environmental changes, and aggregate respondent feedback and evaluation action plans. These technologies also benchmark needs by automatically referencing practices among other (national and international) statistical organizations. Automation supports the collation, analysis, and structuring of these triggers for new or changed statistics, while staff focus their expertise on interpreting context, confirming significance, and ensuring response to complex or emergent requirements.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it requires initial investigation of user needs, identification of what statistics are required, interpretation of environmental changes, and assessment of requirements for new or changed statistical outputs. That needs capability in gathering requirements from clients and stakeholders, researching information needs, analyzing qualitative and quantitative inputs, and helping determine future data requirements. The Junior Evaluation Officer directly fits this need because the role "provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data; gathers and acquires information and analyzes databases," and also "undertakes assigned tasks" such as "identifying, gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data" and participating in "interviews, and focus groups." The role also has communication responsibilities to "discuss data requirements with Statistics Canada clients and evaluation colleagues" and to participate in discussions on "evaluation requirements," which aligns closely with identifying emerging statistical needs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because identifying needs depends on understanding and translating client and program requirements into structured specifications, especially where automated and modernized processes support the collation and structuring of requests. That needs capability to interpret client requirements, assess impacts of changes, and understand program metadata requirements that define what is needed of the statistics. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management in order to develop and translate requirements into specifications" and "interprets client requirements in order to determine options" and possible impacts of modifications. The role also has "knowledge of surveys and statistical programs within Statistics Canada in order to understand program statistical metadata requirements," which is directly relevant when identifying what information products and statistical descriptions are needed.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it includes scanning for new information requests, detecting environmental changes, and structuring triggers for new or changed statistics. That needs capability in gathering information from stakeholders, understanding data requirements, using analytical methods to organize information relevant to study objectives, and supporting exploratory analysis of emerging needs. The Junior Data Analyst fits this because the role "organizes and consolidates information relevant to the defined objectives of studies," "attends Departmental meetings, and interdepartmental and stakeholder meetings (as required), to gather data/information," and "discusses data requirements with operations managers responsible for data collection, other subject matter and systems specialists, clients or service providers." The role also requires knowledge of the data science life cycle including "data capture and acquisition" and "text mining" and "qualitative analysis," which is relevant to modern automated scanning and analysis of user requests.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because identifying needs requires understanding conditions under which statistical operations will occur, changes in data sources or subject areas, and issues that may affect future statistical requirements. That needs capability to meet with clients and specialists, analyze changes affecting outputs, and recommend operational alternatives. The Operations Officer supports this because the role "meets with subject matter and systems specialists, clients, service providers and others, in order to comprehend and elaborate on the conditions within which statistical operations will occur" and has "knowledge of developments and changes in the subject area that may affect the efficiency and validity of data collection, coding and processing." The role also "analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results," which is relevant to recognizing triggers for changed statistics.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it requires identifying new statistical needs by recognizing trends and developments, assessing emerging economic and social issues, and helping translate subject-matter requirements into program implications. That needs capability in trend identification, subject matter review, and feasibility and impact assessment of new or modified statistical programs. Economist/Sociologist 2 directly fits because the role "identifies statistical trends and developments," "participates in subject matter studies and reviews," and liaises "to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development, to suggest improvements to ongoing programs." The role also requires "knowledge of current and emerging economic and social issues relating to the program area in order to identify and assess trends and issues represented by statistical data series" and "knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to conduct studies and to develop/assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because identifying needs includes understanding user information requests and determining the nature and feasibility of statistical outputs required. That needs capability to interpret requests from users, assess potential impacts of new or modified programs, and understand program context and stakeholders. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fits this need because the role "interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations" and in research and analysis "interprets user requests to determine the nature, feasibility, and options for providing the information required." The role also has "knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to prepare information for studies and to review the feasibility and potential impact of new or modified statistical programs" and "knowledge of program context, program sponsors, participants and respondents," all of which directly support identifying what statistics are needed and what is needed of them.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Consult and confirm needs
description: This sub-process focuses on consulting with internal and external stakeholders and confirming in detail the needs for the statistics. Automated and AI-supported systems are now used to organize and analyze input from stakeholders, including feedback, evolving requirements, and historical engagement. These tools facilitate discovery of patterns and highlight changes in user needs over time. Statistical staff engage directly where nuanced negotiation, detailed interpretation, or complex prioritization is required, ensuring that automated summaries and analytics are supplemented by expert, context-aware judgment. This detailed understanding of user needs and the efficient, technology-enabled consultation process are both critical to this sub-process.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it centers on consulting stakeholders and confirming detailed statistical needs, including interpreting feedback, translating requirements, and handling nuanced negotiation and prioritization. That requires roles able to liaise with clients and users, gather and interpret requirements, and convert them into operational or analytical specifications. This work-description directly fits that need because it states the incumbent 'liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development,' and also provides 'data and assistance to users, within and outside Statistics Canada.' Those duties align closely with confirming user needs in detail.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it requires direct consultation with users and stakeholders to understand information needs in detail and determine feasible outputs. That requires capability to interpret client requests, provide consultative services, and assess options for meeting needs. This work-description fills that need because it 'interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations,' 'provides statistical data and consultative services to users,' and in research and analysis 'interprets user requests to determine the nature, feasibility, and options for providing the information required.' These are direct matches to confirming detailed statistical needs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because stakeholder consultation increasingly uses organized feedback and evolving requirements that must be analyzed and translated into specifications. That requires a role able to discuss data requirements with managers, clients, and specialists, gather information in meetings, and support requirement elaboration. This work-description fits because it 'attends Departmental meetings, and interdepartmental and stakeholder meetings (as required), to gather data/information,' 'discusses data requirements with operations managers responsible for data collection, other subject matter and systems specialists, clients or service providers to comprehend and elaborate the conditions within which statistical development and operations will occur,' and 'liaise[s] with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because confirming needs depends on structured consultation with clients and stakeholders, including interviews, focus groups, and analysis of qualitative and quantitative input. That requires a role able to gather stakeholder evidence, participate in consultations, and synthesize requirements. This work-description fills that need because it 'participat[es] in the conduct of interviews, and focus groups,' has speaking skills 'to discuss data requirements with Statistics Canada clients and evaluation colleagues,' is required 'to establish and maintain positive relations with Statistics Canada clients and stakeholders within and outside the Agency,' and 'attends departmental and inter-departmental meetings, when required, to discuss files / issues and evaluation requirements.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because consultation must often result in requirements being translated into metadata specifications, with negotiation of priorities, procedural modifications, and target dates. That requires a role that can liaise with internal clients and interpret requirements in a standards-based environment. This work-description fits because it 'liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management in order to develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata; to negotiate procedural modifications, priorities and target dates,' and 'interprets client requirements in order to determine options for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because detailed consultation with stakeholders must also establish the operational conditions under which statistical collection and processing will occur, and may involve resolving differences that affect quality and efficiency. That requires a role able to meet with clients and service providers, understand issues, and elaborate operational requirements. This work-description fills that need because it 'meets with subject matter and systems specialists, clients, service providers and others, in order to comprehend and elaborate on the conditions within which statistical operations will occur,' and must 'understand the issues and resolve differences that can affect the efficiency of the division's operations and quality of outputs.' It also 'contacts data suppliers or respondents to obtain their collaboration,' which supports stakeholder engagement.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

title: Establish output objectives
description: This sub-process identifies the statistical output objectives that are required to meet the user needs confirmed in sub-process 1.2 (Consult and confirm needs). AI and automated tools aggregate and analyze confirmed user requirements, historical deliverables, legal/normative frameworks, and available resource constraints to generate draft output objectives and candidate quality measures. Staff provide oversight by aligning these drafts with strategic intent, adjudicating complex trade-offs, and ensuring compliance with legal and methodological expectations. This shift supports more efficient, responsive, and high-quality output objective-setting by leveraging technology for foundational work and human expertise for final judgment and alignment.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it requires translating confirmed user needs into concrete statistical output objectives, while also weighing feasibility, quality, strategic alignment, and the implications of methodological and program changes. That requires capability to assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs, analyze how methods and procedures affect outputs, and help translate subject-matter requirements into specifications. Economist/Sociologist 2 directly fills this need because the role "liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development," has "knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to conduct studies and to develop/assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs," and "analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because establishing output objectives depends on interpreting user requirements, determining feasible output options, and assessing how proposed changes will affect data outputs, products, and services. That requires a role able to interpret requests, evaluate feasibility, and connect output design to dissemination realities. Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills that need because the role "interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations," has "knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to prepare information for studies and to review the feasibility and potential impact of new or modified statistical programs," and in analysis work "interprets user requests to determine the nature, feasibility, and options for providing the information required" and "analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because draft output objectives and candidate quality measures must be aligned with documented standards, legal and policy frameworks, and metadata requirements so that outputs are coherent, describable, and quality-assessable. That requires capability to interpret requirements, advise on standards and policies, and evaluate metadata quality implications. Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills that need because the role "provides assistance and advice to internal clients with respect to statistical metadata, documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines," "liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management in order to develop and translate requirements into specifications," and "interprets client requirements in order to determine options for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because AI-generated draft objectives are based on aggregated user requirements, historical deliverables, and resource constraints, and staff must review evidence, organize information relevant to defined objectives, and support methodological choices with analysis. That requires analytical support for consolidating information, assessing data quality and standards, and helping define study objectives. Junior Data Analyst fills that need because the role "organizes and consolidates information relevant to the defined objectives of studies," has knowledge of "data science and its life cycle" including "summarization, reporting, visualization" and "exploratory/ confirmatory, predictive analysis," and has "basic knowledge of theories, principles and techniques of research ... in order to recommend and select project methodologies."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because establishing output objectives includes considering available resource constraints, performance expectations, and evidence on current and future data requirements in order to set realistic and responsive objectives. That requires support in assessing requirements, gathering evidence, and contributing to conclusions about what outputs are needed and justified. Junior Evaluation Officer fills that need because the role "provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data," "identif[ies], gather[s], analyz[es] and synthesiz[es] quantitative and qualitative data," and has knowledge of "program evaluation and performance measurement theories, processes and practices" for "making recommendations concerning the nature and scope of studies and study approaches."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because output objectives must be realistic in light of operational constraints and the conditions under which statistical development and operations will occur. That requires understanding operational methods, system requirements, and how changes to sources and outputs affect integrity and completeness. Operations Officer fills that need because the role "meets with subject matter and systems specialists, clients, service providers and others, in order to comprehend and elaborate on the conditions within which statistical operations will occur," "prepares reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems," and "analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

title: Identify concepts
description: This sub-process clarifies the required concepts to be measured from the point of view of the users. Automated and AI-assisted tools are leveraged to synthesize user requirements, prior documentation, and relevant internal/external sources, providing preliminary suggestions and structured options for possible concepts. The role of the subject matter sponsor is central—this person or group is solely accountable for the final specification and formal certification of the required concepts prior to downstream design or standard alignment. This approach minimizes manual tasks, maintains clear accountability, and increases speed and efficiency in the establishment of robust conceptual frameworks.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it requires clarifying and specifying the concepts to be measured from the users' point of view, synthesizing requirements and prior sources, and translating subject-matter needs into defined conceptual specifications before later design work. That requires subject-matter analytical capability, understanding of concepts and definitions, and the ability to work with users and other specialists to turn requirements into specifications. This work-description directly fits that need because it explicitly states that the incumbent "liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development," and "writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology." It also includes the ability to "assess[] and determine[] the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored," which is directly relevant to identifying and refining required concepts.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because identifying concepts depends on understanding user requirements, gathering relevant information, and synthesizing qualitative and quantitative evidence from documentation and stakeholders into preliminary conceptual options. That requires research, synthesis, interviews/focus groups, and support to assess requirements. This work-description fits because it "undertakes assigned tasks related to specific elements of evaluation projects such as, conducting literature and data research, identifying, gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data; participating in the conduct of interviews, and focus groups," and "provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data." Those activities align closely with the phase description's emphasis on synthesizing user requirements and relevant internal/external sources to clarify concepts.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because concept identification requires interpreting user needs, organizing relevant information around defined objectives, and translating subject-matter requirements into usable specifications. It also benefits from analytical support that can synthesize inputs from multiple sources. This work-description fits because it states that the incumbent "organizes and consolidates information relevant to the defined objectives of studies," "discusses data requirements with operations managers responsible for data collection, other subject matter and systems specialists, clients or service providers to comprehend and elaborate the conditions within which statistical development and operations will occur," and "liaise[s] with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development." Those are directly relevant to clarifying concepts from the users' perspective.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because once concepts are being identified, they often need to be expressed in structured metadata and aligned with documented standards, frameworks, and policies so they can be formally specified and used downstream. That requires knowledge of statistical metadata concepts and the ability to translate requirements into metadata specifications. This work-description fits because it "liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management in order to develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata," and requires "knowledge of statistical metadata concepts and frameworks used within Statistics Canada, the Government of Canada and internationally." It also notes "knowledge of survey and statistical program subject matter concepts and methodologies" to assess client requirements, which supports formal conceptual clarification and standard alignment preparation.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because identifying concepts requires interaction with users and specialists to elaborate the conditions under which statistical operations will occur, and to clarify statistical concepts that will later guide collection and processing. That requires operational understanding of statistical concepts and the ability to explain and refine them with stakeholders. This work-description fits because it includes meeting "with subject matter and systems specialists, clients, service providers and others, in order to comprehend and elaborate on the conditions within which statistical operations will occur," and contacting respondents or suppliers "to clarify and explain statistical concepts." It also includes "knowledge of the underlying statistical and economic principles and concepts required for the collection, coding and processing of data," which supports concept clarification before downstream operational design.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because concept identification must reflect user information needs and subject-matter requirements in forms that can later support data products and dissemination. That requires interpreting user requests, understanding subject-matter concepts, and helping translate requirements into specifications. This work-description fits because it "liaises with other specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development," and "interprets client information requests" while applying "knowledge of the socio-economic concepts and methods" and "knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to prepare information for studies and to review the feasibility and potential impact of new or modified statistical programs." These capabilities support the clarification of concepts from the user perspective.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Check data availability and suitability
description: This sub-process systematically checks whether current sources of data could meet user requirements and the conditions under which they would be available, including any restrictions on their use. Existing data holdings must be exhaustively investigated and prioritized first, followed by a search for relevant administrative and alternative data sources; the option to conduct new surveys is only considered if these avenues prove insufficient to meet data needs. The subject matter sponsor holds sole accountability for certifying that all relevant avenues for data have been thoroughly explored and that the suitability, timeliness, and quality of any proposed source have been rigorously assessed. To expedite and strengthen the acquisition of administrative and alternative data, a center of expertise works collaboratively with subject matter specialists to support negotiations, acquisition logistics, and the establishment of legal or operational agreements where needed. When multiple avenues have been assessed and documented, a strategy for filling any remaining gaps is prepared. This sub-process also encompasses the assessment and possible updates to the legal framework for data collection, ensuring fit-for-purpose, respondent-efficient, and timely data acquisition and usage.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it requires systematically investigating existing data holdings and other possible sources, assessing whether they meet user requirements, and judging suitability, timeliness, quality, availability conditions, and restrictions on use. That requires capability to identify accessible sources, gather and analyze information from multiple sources, and assess current and future data requirements. This work-description directly fills that need because it states the incumbent "Provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data; gathers and acquires information and analyzes databases" and "identifies and recommends to the Evaluation Manager the usefulness and accessible sources of data to be used in studies." It also notes communication with clients and outside professionals "to obtain data" and participation in discussions on "data requirements," which aligns with checking whether available sources can meet needs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because checking data availability and suitability depends on understanding source documentation, metadata quality, policy constraints, and how data holdings can be interpreted against user requirements. That requires capability to interpret requirements, evaluate metadata quality, and apply policies and legal directives relevant to data use. This work-description fills that need because it "provides assistance and advice to internal clients with respect to statistical metadata, documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines," "assists with statistical metadata quality evaluations," and "interprets client requirements in order to determine options for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata." Its knowledge of "the Statistics Act" and awareness of "the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of statistical information" also supports the phase's emphasis on restrictions on use and legal framework considerations.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it requires assessing candidate data sources for quality, origin, integrity, and fitness for use before deciding whether existing, administrative, or alternative data can satisfy requirements. That requires capability in data acquisition, data preparation, quality assessment, and risk assessment across varied sources. This work-description directly supports that need because it includes knowledge of the data science life cycle including "data capture and acquisition," and the incumbent "conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin." It also requires "knowledge of techniques and methods of information collection and analysis, evolving information sources, survey methodologies, data risk assessment" and knowledge of partnerships "to assess data provided by other levels of government for validity and integrity," which is highly relevant to evaluating administrative and alternative sources.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because evaluating whether data sources are available and suitable includes understanding operational conditions for collection and processing, verifying source reliability, and considering legal and procedural constraints on obtaining data. That requires capability to analyze data sources, assess impacts of source changes, work with suppliers, and understand statutory requirements governing collection and use. This work-description fills that need because it includes "Knowledge of data sources and contacts within Statistics Canada" and external contacts "to obtain collaboration in the provision of statistical information and to verify the accuracy of data." It also states the incumbent "Analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results" and has knowledge of "the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts" to ensure application in "the collection, coding and processing of data," which aligns with assessing availability conditions and legal framework issues.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it centers on subject-matter assessment of whether available sources are relevant, feasible, and adequate, including the constraints arising from concepts, definitions, collection conditions, and program context. That requires capability to assess feasibility and impact of data options, understand the survey universe and sponsors, and analyze how collection conditions affect results. This work-description directly fills that need because it includes "Knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to conduct studies and to develop/assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs," as well as "Knowledge of the subject and universe of the survey" and "Knowledge of program context, program sponsors, participants and respondents to plan and organize the retrieval and processing of data for research or development projects." It further states the incumbent "Assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored," which is central to suitability assessment.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because checking data availability and suitability requires compiling data from diverse sources, determining feasibility of meeting user requests, and evaluating consistency, reliability, and appropriateness of candidate data. That requires capability to interpret user requirements, assess data quality, and compare internal sources. This work-description fills that need because it states the incumbent "Interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations," "Reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases," and "Compiles data from diverse sources" while "Analyz[ing] and evaluat[ing] data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness." It also includes "Interprets user requests to determine the nature, feasibility, and options for providing the information required" and knowledge of "data sources within Statistics Canada," directly matching the need to investigate and prioritize existing holdings and assess whether they can satisfy requirements.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Prepare and submit business case
description: This sub-process documents the findings of the other sub-processes in this phase in the form of a business case to get approval to implement a new or modified statistical business process. In the contemporary process, automated and AI-driven systems are used to collate, analyze, and generate initial drafts for all key business case sections—including the description of the 'As-Is' process, the proposed 'To-Be' solution, and the relevant assessments of cost, benefit, risks, deliverables, and impact. Staff and sponsors then review, contextualize, and refine these drafts, ensuring proper alignment with strategic objectives and organizational needs before final submission. The business case is reviewed and approved by the relevant body, with human expertise providing the final evaluation and decision. By leveraging automation, the preparation of business cases gains efficiency and speed, allowing human effort to be concentrated on strategic oversight and quality assurance.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it requires documenting findings from earlier work into a formal business case, including assessments of cost, benefit, risks, deliverables, impact, and alignment with organizational objectives. That creates a need for capability in evaluation, socio-economic and cost-benefit analysis, synthesis of qualitative and quantitative evidence, and preparation of briefing/report material for senior management. The Junior Evaluation Officer directly fills this need because the role "participates as a member of project teams in the conduct of evaluation studies related to programs, policies and initiatives," "identifying, gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data," and "provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data" while also participating in "socio-economic analyses and cost-benefit analysis of programs." The role also "provides the Evaluation Manager with supporting data for sections of reports, presentations, briefing notes and memoranda for senior management," which closely matches preparing business case content for approval.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because a business case for a new or modified statistical business process must assess feasibility, impact, procedural change, and implications of alternative methods before approval. That requires capability to review the feasibility and potential impact of modified statistical programs, compile and assess evidence, and support preparation of analytical material. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role has "knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to prepare information for studies and to review the feasibility and potential impact of new or modified statistical programs." It also "compiles data from diverse sources," "analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness," and "analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services," all of which are directly relevant to drafting and substantiating business case sections on impacts, options, and deliverables.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because the business case must describe the current 'As-Is' process, the proposed 'To-Be' solution, operational requirements, and risks or impacts of implementation. That creates a need for operational analysis, articulation of options and requirements, and reporting on how statistical operations function and would change. The Operations Officer fills this need because the role "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives" and "prepares reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems." The role also "meets with subject matter and systems specialists, clients, service providers and others, in order to comprehend and elaborate on the conditions within which statistical operations will occur" and "assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems," which directly supports business case development for modified processes.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because preparing a business case requires analysis of proposed changes to methods, procedures, systems, and outputs, along with articulation of feasibility, impact, and program implications for decision-makers. That requires subject-matter analytical capability and the ability to assess new or modified statistical programs. Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role includes "knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to conduct studies and to develop/assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs." It also "analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services" and liaises with others "to establish project plans, priorities and target dates," which aligns with business case content on impacts, implementation planning, and organizational fit.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because automated and AI-driven drafting of business case sections still depends on collating, analyzing, and organizing evidence on current processes, proposed changes, risks, and decision-relevant impacts. That creates a need for data preparation, quantitative analysis, organization of information to defined objectives, and preparation of analytical reports and briefings. The Junior Data Analyst fills this need because the role "supports the conduct of studies and/or projects using established quantitative statistical data analysis methods," "conducts data preparation techniques" including extraction, cleansing, transformation, validation, and quality assessment, and "organizes and consolidates information relevant to the defined objectives of studies." The role also has "writing skills ... to draft clear and simple analytical reports, briefings and presentation material," which supports evidence assembly and draft business case preparation.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because a business case for a modified statistical business process may need to document metadata implications, procedural changes, quality considerations, and impacts of new methods or systems on documentation and dissemination. That requires capability to analyze proposed modifications, translate requirements into specifications, and contribute to reports and documentation. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata," "interprets client requirements in order to determine options" and possible impacts of proposed modifications, and "analyzes current production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation methods, procedures and systems in order to propose enhancements or alternatives." The role also "contributes written information to be used as input to reports" and documentation, which is directly relevant to preparing business case sections concerning metadata-related process changes.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Design
description: This phase describes the development and design activities, and any associated practical research work needed to define the statistical outputs, variables, methodologies, collection instruments, and operational processes—with a strong emphasis on automation, AI-powered tools, and digital interoperability. Automated and AI-driven processes play a central role in drafting specifications, aligning with corporate and international standards, generating and enriching metadata, simulating system interactions, and iterating design improvements. All statistical products and their supporting metadata are produced in standardized, richly described, and machine-actionable forms, ensuring they are interoperable and reusable across downstream tools, APIs, and organizational systems. Staff are freed from repetitive and routine design work and instead focus on innovation, calibration, and optimizing for evolving user and stakeholder requirements. Design activities thus promote efficiency, quality, and discoverability, embedding best practices for automation, standardization, and open data access. The Design phase is broken down into six sub-processes (Figure 8), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, can occur in parallel, and may be iterative. Iteration between Design and Build phases is supported through automated versioning and process enhancements.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The phase is implicating because Design requires defining statistical outputs, variables, methodologies, collection instruments, operational processes, and specifications, while aligning these with standards, automation, interoperability, and evolving user requirements. This needs roles that can translate subject-matter and client requirements into specifications, assess and improve methods and procedures, and support the design of statistical processes and systems. Economist/Sociologist 2 directly fills this need because it "liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development," and has "knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to conduct studies and to develop/assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs." It also "analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems," which is central to design work.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The phase is implicating because Design emphasizes standardized, richly described, machine-actionable metadata, as well as alignment with corporate and international standards and the generation and enrichment of metadata. This needs a role specialized in metadata frameworks, metadata specifications, metadata quality, and metadata production and dissemination procedures. Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because it "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata," "liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management in order to develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata," and has "knowledge of statistical metadata concepts and frameworks used within Statistics Canada, the Government of Canada and internationally." The role also "provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures" and "participates in the testing of new procedures and systems," which supports iterative design.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The phase is implicating because Design includes defining methodologies, variables, outputs, and operational processes with strong emphasis on automation, AI-powered tools, and digital interoperability. This needs analytical and data-oriented capability to support data development specifications, assess standards conformity, and contribute to methodological and technical design. Junior Data Analyst fills this need because it supports studies using quantitative methods and software such as "Python, SAS, STATA, R," conducts "data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin," and "liaise[s] with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development." Its knowledge of the "data science life cycle" and of "model design and interpretation" is directly relevant to design activities involving automation and AI-enabled processes.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The phase is implicating because Design must define collection instruments and operational processes, and support iteration into Build through specifications, testing considerations, and process enhancements. This needs a role that understands collection, coding, processing operations, and can assess system requirements and operational implications. Operations Officer fills this need because it "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives," and has "knowledge of systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows, general software packages and computer languages, for designing the specifications for testing of applications." It also "assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems," which is directly implicated in design.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The phase is implicating because Design includes defining statistical outputs and ensuring they are reusable, interoperable, and responsive to user and stakeholder requirements. This needs a role that can interpret user requirements, assess feasibility of outputs, and examine how revised processing specifications affect downstream data products and services. Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because it "liaises with other specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development," "interprets user requests to determine the nature, feasibility, and options for providing the information required," and "examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems." Those duties directly support design of outputs and interoperable processes.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The phase is implicating because Design includes practical research work needed to define methodologies, optimize for evolving user and stakeholder requirements, and improve methods and processes. This needs research support to identify data requirements, analyze evidence, and recommend enhancements to methods. Junior Evaluation Officer fills this need because it "provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data," "undertakes literature and data research," and "recommends to the Evaluation Manager, enhancements to methods for retrieving data as well as information used in the conduct of socio-economic analyses and cost-benefit analyses." While not a primary design role for statistical production systems, it is directly implicated in the research and requirements-assessment aspects of the phase.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

title: Design outputs and dissemination
description: This sub-process contains the detailed design of the statistical outputs, products, and services to be produced, including all systems, tools, and procedures to be used in dissemination. Automated and AI-supported solutions are used wherever possible to produce initial output templates, align with existing standards, generate metadata, and configure dissemination tools, allowing staff to focus on innovative features and context-specific requirements, including confidentiality. All outputs and dissemination artifacts must be standardized, richly described, and machine-actionable, with support for APIs, comprehensive metadata tagging, and open formats to maximize interoperability, discoverability, and reusability by human and machine clients. The process includes an explicit, early review of the type and necessity of products, especially visualizations, with the expectation that only those genuinely required for user value or compliance are designed—allowing exclusion where end-users can self-serve or alternatives suffice. Outputs may also be designed in partnership with external organizations, ensuring full alignment with digital-to-digital workflows and standards.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it requires the detailed design of dissemination outputs and artifacts, with strong emphasis on metadata generation, standards alignment, machine-actionable description, dissemination tools, and confidentiality-aware dissemination. That requires capability to produce, validate, store, disseminate, and evaluate statistical metadata, and to translate client and program requirements into metadata and dissemination specifications. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the role 'prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository,' 'provides assistance and advice to internal clients with respect to statistical metadata, documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines,' and 'provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata.' The role also explicitly supports standards, systems, and dissemination design through knowledge of 'statistical metadata concepts and frameworks,' 'methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata,' and awareness of 'security and confidentiality of statistical information.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it covers the detailed design of statistical outputs, products, services, and dissemination procedures, including tailoring outputs to user needs, configuring dissemination approaches, and ensuring outputs are suitable for publication and reuse. That requires capability in producing and disseminating statistical data products, interpreting user requests, adapting outputs to formats, and assessing effects of procedural or system changes on outputs, products, and services. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the role 'edits, validates, markets and disseminates data,' 'interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations,' and 'provides statistical data and consultative services to users.' It also supports output design through research and analysis activities that 'compile[] data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output,' 'interpret[] user requests to determine the nature, feasibility, and options for providing the information required,' and 'adapt[] data to new definitions or presentation formats.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it explicitly includes designing outputs and products such as visualizations, standardized artifacts, and dissemination-ready materials, while reviewing whether particular products are necessary for user value. That requires capability to prepare analytical outputs, visualizations, dashboards, and presentation materials that communicate data clearly and appropriately to varied audiences. The Junior Data Analyst is implicated because the role includes knowledge of the data science life cycle including 'summarization, reporting, visualization, business intelligence,' and states that 'writing skills are necessary to draft clear and simple analytical reports, briefings and presentation material using data visualization tools for managers and clients with varying levels of knowledge and understanding of data science.' The role also supports standards-conformant output preparation through 'data preparation techniques' including 'data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because output and dissemination design includes specifying systems, tools, and procedures, and ensuring outputs remain aligned with standards, workflows, and operational realities. That requires capability to translate subject-matter requirements into system specifications and to assess how changes in procedures and technology affect outputs, products, and services. Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role 'liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development,' and its research responsibilities include 'analyz[ing] changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services' and 'analyz[ing] current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.' This directly supports design decisions about what outputs should be produced and how they should be presented and disseminated.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because dissemination design includes the design of output artifacts such as tables, charts, graphs, and explanatory text, as well as the procedures and system requirements that support regular and ad hoc publication. That requires capability to prepare publication-oriented output formats and to assess operational system requirements affecting outputs. The Operations Officer is relevant because the role 'designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text for use in regular and ad-hoc publications' and 'prepares reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems.' The role also 'analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results,' which supports dissemination design choices tied to output quality and operational feasibility.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

title: Design variables
description: This sub-process defines the variables to be collected via the collection instrument and any that will be derived for analysis or dissemination, with a strong emphasis on standards compliance, automation, and machine-actionability. All variable definitions and supporting metadata must comply with national and international standards (e.g., SDMX), structured in machine-actionable formats and managed through prescribed data management tools (such as Aria or Colectica) to ensure robust lifecycle control and digital traceability. AI/LLM-enabled tools are used to generate, refine, and validate variable names, descriptions, and attributes, maximizing clarity, standardization, and discoverability. Staff involved in this sub-process are proficient in digital metadata standards and tooling, ensuring all variable-related products are interoperable, automation-ready, and reusable by both human and machine users. This ensures that the resulting statistical outputs are consistently described, easily found, and seamlessly integrated across digital platforms and systems.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it explicitly requires defining variables and their supporting metadata in compliance with standards, in machine-actionable formats, and within metadata management tools so they are interoperable, reusable, and traceable. That creates a need for capability in statistical metadata concepts, standards, validation, storage, dissemination, metadata quality evaluation, and use of metadata software. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills that need because the role "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository," and has "knowledge of statistical metadata concepts and frameworks used within Statistics Canada, the Government of Canada and internationally" as well as "knowledge of software used in the production, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata." The role also "provides assistance and advice to internal clients with respect to statistical metadata, documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines," which aligns directly with standards-compliant variable design.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because variable design must specify variables for collection, derivation, analysis, and dissemination in ways that support automation and downstream processing. That requires translating subject-matter requirements into specifications, assessing concepts and definitions, and analyzing how methods and procedures affect outputs. Economist/Sociologist 2 fills that need because the role "liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development," and includes writing "detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology." It also has "knowledge of the subject and universe of the survey" and "analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems," which is directly relevant to defining meaningful, usable variables.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because variables must be designed so they can be collected through instruments and used in automated collection, coding, and processing operations. That creates a need to understand collection specifications, data flows, coding and processing implications, and how concepts and definitions are implemented operationally. The Operations Officer fills that need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives," and "meets with subject matter and systems specialists... in order to comprehend and elaborate on the conditions within which statistical operations will occur." The role also has "knowledge of systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows," which supports automation-ready variable design.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because variables are not only collected but also derived for analysis and dissemination, and therefore must be designed to support data quality, transformation, conformity to standards, and analytical usability. That creates a need for expertise in data preparation, validation, standards conformity, and the broader data life cycle. The Junior Data Analyst fills that need because the role "conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin." The role also requires "knowledge of data science and its life cycle" including "data capture and acquisition... cleansing, processing... summarization, reporting, visualization," and "knowledge of techniques and methods of information collection and analysis... in order to assess the quality of data and identify and mitigate risks to its integrity." These capabilities support designing variables that are analysis-ready and automation-ready.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because variables must ultimately support dissemination and be consistently described and discoverable across systems, which requires attention to definitions, formats, user requirements, and adaptation of data structures for output products. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills that need because the role "liaises with other specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development," and "adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats." It also "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases" and has knowledge of "methods, techniques, practices and procedures to prepare information for studies and to review the feasibility and potential impact of new or modified statistical programs." This supports designing variables that can be effectively used in dissemination products and custom outputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Design collection
description: This sub-process prepares a collection strategy for the data and determines the most appropriate collection instruments and methods, with a strategic emphasis on automation, AI/ML, and passive acquisition. Where possible, the design must prioritize passive, administrative, and already-available sources of data; surveys or direct solicitation are employed only when all other avenues are exhausted or cannot provide suitable data. All aspects of collection design—including the configuration of instruments, sequencing, respondent communications, and integration agreements—should embed automation, machine-to-machine interfaces, digital event/trigger-based collection, and minimal manual intervention. Where a survey instrument is essential, automated and AI-driven methods must be used for design, rendering, and fielding, ensuring quick turnaround, reduced burden, and full standards compliance. The sub-process also entails the necessary design of respondent management, monitoring, and adaptive feedback loops to maximize efficiency and data quality, while reserving human staff for exception handling and final validation.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it is explicitly about designing collection strategy, instruments, methods, respondent communications, monitoring, and operational approaches, with emphasis on automation and minimal manual intervention. That requires a role able to work directly on collection operations, evaluate collection methods and procedures, and translate operational conditions into system and process requirements. The Operations Officer directly fills this need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives," and "provides assistance and advice to users on methods and practices of collection and coding." The work description also shows design-relevant capability through "prepares reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems," meeting with specialists and service providers "to comprehend and elaborate on the conditions within which statistical operations will occur," and assessing "system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers".
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because collection design must prioritize passive, administrative, and already-available data sources before resorting to surveys, and must support automation, data capture, acquisition, and quality-aware collection methods. That requires capability in data acquisition life cycle, information collection methods, survey methodologies, and translating requirements into specifications. The Junior Data Analyst fills this need because the role has knowledge of "data science and its life cycle, including data capture and acquisition," as well as "knowledge of techniques and methods of information collection and analysis, evolving information sources, survey methodologies, data risk assessment, impact and quantitative analysis in order to assess the quality of data and identify and mitigate risks to its integrity." The role also "discusses data requirements with operations managers responsible for data collection, other subject matter and systems specialists" and "liaise[s] with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development," which is directly relevant to designing collection approaches and automated acquisition arrangements.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because designing collection includes selecting and refining collection, processing, editing, and related methods and procedures, and ensuring they are relevant, efficient, and suitable for the survey or statistical program context. That requires subject-matter capability to assess collection methods and propose alternatives or improvements.
