Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role "participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities." The work description further supports direct implication through "liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development," and through research functions that "analyze current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because collection design must ensure standards compliance and proper configuration of instruments, methods, and related documentation, especially where automated or AI-driven survey instruments are used. That creates a need for metadata support so collection instruments and processes are documented, validated, and aligned with standards and policies. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills that need because the role "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata," provides "assistance and advice to internal clients with respect to statistical metadata, documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines," and "liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management in order to develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata." The role also has "knowledge of survey and statistical program subject matter concepts and methodologies relevant to the collection... of data," which directly supports collection design documentation and standards compliance.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because collection design includes determining the most appropriate sources of data and methods for obtaining them, especially prioritizing already-available and alternative sources before direct collection. That requires identifying useful and accessible data sources and supporting data acquisition decisions. The Junior Evaluation Officer is implicated because the role "provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data; gathers and acquires information and analyzes databases," and "identifies and recommends to the Evaluation Manager the usefulness and accessible sources of data to be used in studies." The work description also notes communication with clients "in the data acquisition process" and knowledge used to carry out "data research, collection and compilation assignments," which aligns with source selection and collection strategy design.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

title: Design frame and sample
description: This sub-process, which applies to all statistical processes involving sampling, is built around digital automation, flexibility, and data quality by design. Whenever frames or registers from administrative, alternative, or partner-held sources are used, partners are expected and supported to apply AI-driven data cleaning and quality control processes prior to data ingestion by Statistics Canada—improving coverage, comparability, and downstream analytic value. The specification of the population of interest, development of the sampling frame, and establishment of sampling criteria and methodology are designed for full integration with end-to-end digital pipelines, supporting automated and seamless flow between pre-collection and post-collection business processes, drastically reducing manual involvement and risk of programmatic 'patches.' Sampling designs must explicitly allow for a range of dynamic and flexible options (including person-based and adaptive sampling), with supporting digital tools enabling real-time optimization informed by diverse data realities and program goals. This ensures the most efficient, quality-driven, and responsive sampling methodologies possible.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it requires specifying the population of interest, developing sampling frames, establishing sampling criteria and methodology, and ensuring those designs work within automated digital pipelines with strong data quality controls. That creates a need for capability in statistical sampling, data preparation, data quality assessment, and translating subject-matter requirements into data development specifications. The Junior Data Analyst directly fits this need because the role includes 'data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin,' and requires knowledge of 'data science and its life cycle, including data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing' as well as 'survey methodologies, data risk assessment' and 'statistical sampling.' The role also 'discusses data requirements with operations managers responsible for data collection, other subject matter and systems specialists' and 'develop[s] and translate[s] subject matter requirements into specifications for data development,' which is directly relevant to frame and sample design integrated with digital pipelines.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because designing frames and samples depends on understanding data sources, assessing their integrity and completeness, and ensuring operational compatibility between sampling design and downstream collection and processing systems. That creates a need for operational knowledge of data sources, verification methods, system requirements, and impacts of changes to sources and outputs. The Operations Officer fills this need because the role 'participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data,' 'evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives,' and has knowledge of 'methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications.' The role also 'analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results' and 'assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers,' which aligns with building sampling frames from administrative or partner-held sources and integrating them into end-to-end automated processes.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because frame and sample design requires methodological assessment of the survey universe, the effects of concepts and definitions on results, and the suitability of changes to statistical methods and procedures. That creates a need for subject-matter and methodological capability to assess feasibility, validity, and impacts of alternative statistical approaches. Economist/Sociologist 2 fits this need because the role includes 'participat[ing] in the analysis of data and suggest[ing] possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.' The role also requires 'knowledge of statistical or economic theory and principles ... and the methods and techniques of data gathering, statistical estimation,' 'knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to conduct studies and to develop/assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs,' and 'knowledge of the subject and universe of the survey ... in order to propose suitable changes to statistical or reporting methods and techniques.' Those capabilities are directly implicated in specifying populations, designing frames, and selecting sampling methodologies.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because digital frame and sample design requires clear metadata and documented specifications so that population definitions, frame structures, sampling criteria, and methodological choices can be consistently implemented across automated pipelines. That creates a need for metadata production, validation, quality evaluation, and translation of requirements into specifications. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills that need because the role 'prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata,' 'liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management in order to develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata,' and has knowledge of 'survey and statistical program subject matter concepts and methodologies relevant to the collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data.' The role also 'interprets client requirements' and 'evaluates selected indicators of statistical metadata quality,' which supports the documented, quality-by-design implementation of frame and sample specifications in digital systems.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Design processing and analysis
description: This sub-process designs the statistical methodology to be applied during the Process and Analyse phases, with a core emphasis on standards-based automation, AI enablement, and digital interoperability. Specifications for routines and rules covering coding, editing, imputation, validation, and data integration/estimation are required to be implemented, where practical, using automated frameworks and AI/ML-driven tools—leveraging SDMX models, .STAT processing, and corporate-standard solutions (e.g., Aria/Colectica). Human analysts and methodologists are focused on reviewing and updating analytic methods for non-standard or novel use-cases, with all standardizable and repeatable components digital, automated, and reproducible by default. Statistical disclosure control and quality assurance methods designed here also leverage automation and AI for rapid, secure, and scalable deployment. All methodologies are documented to be compatible with downstream digital workflows and to support auditing, versioning, and continuous improvement.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it requires the design of processing and analysis methodologies, including specifications for coding, editing, validation, data integration and estimation, with emphasis on automation, reproducibility, and compatibility with downstream systems. This needs roles that can translate subject-matter requirements into system specifications, analyze and improve processing methods, and assess impacts of methodological and technological changes. Economist/Sociologist 2 directly fills this need because the work-description states that the role 'liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development,' and 'analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.' It also includes 'knowledge of statistical or economic theory and principles ... and the methods and techniques of data gathering, statistical estimation and economic modeling,' which aligns with designing processing and analysis methodology.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it centers on designing operational processing rules and specifications for coding, editing, validation, and automated processing workflows. This requires capability in collection/coding/processing operations, systems analysis, testing specifications, and ensuring reliability and consistency to specifications. Operations Officer fills that need because the role 'participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data,' 'evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives,' and has 'knowledge of systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows, general software packages and computer languages, for designing the specifications for testing of applications.' The role also 'assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems,' which is directly relevant to designing processing methods for later implementation.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it requires design of data preparation, cleansing, transformation, validation, modeling, and AI/ML-enabled analytical workflows that are automated and reproducible. This needs a role with practical knowledge of the data science lifecycle and hands-on experience with data preparation and analytical software. Junior Data Analyst fills that need because the work-description says the role 'supports the conduct of studies and/or projects using established quantitative statistical data analysis methods and software such as Python, SAS, STATA, R,' and 'conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin.' It also explicitly includes 'knowledge of data science and its life cycle, including ... cleansing, processing, mining, clustering, modeling, summarization' and 'predictive analysis,' which strongly aligns with the phase's emphasis on automated and AI-enabled processing and analysis design.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it requires methodologies to be standards-based, digitally interoperable, documented, and compatible with downstream workflows, including use of corporate-standard solutions and metadata-aware processing. This creates a need for expertise in statistical metadata concepts, standards, validation, and translating requirements into metadata specifications. Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills that need because the role 'prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata,' 'liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management in order to develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata,' and has 'knowledge of statistical metadata concepts and frameworks ... and how those concepts and frameworks are used and reflected in policies, methods and procedures.' The role also 'analyzes current production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation methods, procedures and systems in order to propose enhancements or alternatives,' supporting the design of interoperable and documented processing frameworks.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it includes designing editing, validation, and quality assurance methods and ensuring that revised processing specifications work coherently with broader data capture and processing functions. This requires a role that works directly with edited and validated data, reviews quality impacts from systems and databases, and examines revised processing specifications. Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills that need because the role 'edits, validates ... data,' 'reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases,' and 'examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems.' It also 'analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output,' which is directly relevant to designing robust processing and analysis methods.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it involves reviewing and updating analytic methods for non-standard or novel use-cases and designing methodologies that support analysis in later phases. This requires analytical capability to interpret data, apply analytical tools, and recommend enhancements to methods. Junior Evaluation Officer is implicated because the role 'undertakes assigned tasks related to specific elements of evaluation projects such as ... analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data; ... applying analytical tools and techniques to determine implications of evaluation results,' and 'provides input on the interpretation of data to support findings and conclusions.' The role also 'recommends ... enhancements to methods for retrieving data as well as information used in the conduct of socio-economic analyses and cost-benefit analyses,' which aligns with contributing to method design and refinement, especially for less standard analytical cases.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

title: Design production systems and workflows
description: This sub-process determines the workflow from data collection to dissemination, ensuring all production processes are seamlessly integrated, modular, and event-driven, with automation and AI/ML supporting orchestration, monitoring, and transitions. Workflows are designed to minimize manual intervention and maximize real-time coordination, leveraging digital platforms and automation for every routine or standardized task. The emphasis is on building touchless, continuous data pipelines that allow for automated validation, routing, escalation, and exception reporting. Existing automated solutions and system components are reused wherever possible; if new components are needed, they are built automation- and integration-ready from inception. Staff responsibilities focus on system oversight, addressing exceptions and inefficiencies, and iteratively improving and upgrading automated workflows for future resilience and scalability.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it explicitly requires designing end-to-end workflows from collection through dissemination, with integrated production processes, automation, monitoring, validation, routing, and iterative workflow improvement. That requires roles able to work across collection, coding, processing, operational systems, and testing/specification of applications. The Operations Officer directly fits this need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," has "knowledge of systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows," and "assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems." The role also "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives," which aligns with improving and upgrading workflows.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it covers workflow design across the full production chain and stresses integration of data capture, processing, and dissemination components. That requires roles that can assess how revised processing specifications affect coordination among systems and outputs. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases" and, crucially, "examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems." The role also "liaises with other specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development," directly supporting workflow and system design.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it emphasizes automation-ready, integrated workflows, reuse of components, and iterative improvement of production methods and procedures. That requires roles that analyze current collection, processing, editing, compilation, and presentation methods and translate subject-matter requirements into system specifications. Economist/Sociologist 2 fits this because the role "liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development," and "analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems." It also "analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services," which supports resilient workflow design.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because designing touchless, continuous data pipelines depends on capabilities in data extraction, cleansing, transformation, validation, standards conformance, and translating operational requirements into data development specifications. The Junior Data Analyst fills this need because the role "conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin." The role also includes knowledge of the data science life cycle, including "data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing" and communication responsibilities to "discuss data requirements with operations managers responsible for data collection, other subject matter and systems specialists" and to "develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development." These are directly relevant to workflow design and automation-ready pipelines.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because integrated production workflows from collection to dissemination also depend on metadata production, storage, dissemination, quality evaluation, and adaptation of metadata procedures and systems as workflows change. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata; and participates in the testing of new procedures and systems." It also "liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management in order to develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata," and "analyzes current production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation methods, procedures and systems in order to propose enhancements or alternatives." This directly supports modular, integrated workflow design.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Build
description: This phase builds and tests the production solution to the point where it is ready for use in the 'live' environment, leveraging modular automation and AI-driven assembly at every step. The outputs of the Design phase are assembled and configured using digital orchestration pipelines that prioritize reusability, traceability, and compliance with business architecture and security requirements. Automated configuration, integration, and self-testing are employed wherever possible, enabling rapid, reliable, and consistent system deployment. Human expertise is reserved for overseeing automated processes, handling exceptions that cannot be resolved by automation, and driving continuous improvement in modular service creation. New services are developed only to fill gaps, and are built from inception for automation compatibility, modularity, and compliance. The Build phase is structured into seven sub-processes (Figure 9), supporting iteration and parallelization, and is tightly integrated with Design to ensure seamless translation of specifications into robust operational environments.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The phase is implicating because it centers on assembling, configuring, integrating, testing, and preparing production solutions for live use, with emphasis on automation, traceability, compliance, and deployment readiness. This requires roles that can translate requirements into build specifications, participate in testing, assess system impacts, and support operational implementation of production processes. The Operations Officer directly fits this need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," has "knowledge of systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows," and specifically "assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems." The role also supports build verification through responsibilities for "designing the specifications for testing of applications" and preparing reports on operational requirements.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The phase is implicating because Build requires the outputs of Design to be assembled into operational environments through configuration, integration, testing, and controlled deployment, while maintaining compliance and reusability. This creates a need for roles that can translate subject-matter requirements into system specifications and assess how revised processing specifications affect integrated production functions. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "liaises with other specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development," and "examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems." That directly supports build assembly, integration, and readiness of production solutions.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The phase is implicating because Build depends on converting design requirements into configured production components, testing new procedures and systems, and ensuring traceable, compliant operational metadata support. This requires capability in metadata production, validation, testing, and adaptation of documentation and procedures when systems change. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer is directly implicated because the role "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository," "participates in the testing of new procedures and systems," and "analyzes changes in methods, procedures and systems used to produce, store, disseminate and evaluate the quality of statistical metadata in order to determine the need to update statistical metadata or adapt it to new formats." The role also supports compliance because it requires awareness of "the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of statistical information to ensure that actions are in compliance."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The phase is implicating because Build includes assembling and testing production-ready solutions and ensuring that data processing components operate reliably in the target environment. This requires roles able to support data preparation, validation, conformity to standards, and translation of requirements into specifications for development and operations. The Junior Data Analyst fits this need because the role "conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin," and "liaise[s] with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development." The role's knowledge of the data science life cycle, including "capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing" and governance for protecting data assets, supports build activities involving configured and tested data pipelines.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The phase is implicating because Build requires seamless translation of specifications into operational environments, including procedural modifications, project plans, priorities, and target dates for system development. This creates a need for subject-matter roles that can help define specifications and assess effects of changes in procedures and technology on outputs. Economist/Sociologist 2 is implicated because the role "liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development, to suggest improvements to ongoing programs, to negotiate procedural modifications and to establish project plans, priorities and target dates." It also supports build assessment by "analyz[ing] changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

title: Reuse or build collection instruments
description: This sub-process describes the activities to build and reuse the collection instruments needed during the Collect phase. Subject matter sponsors are solely responsible for specifying and certifying collection instrument requirements. The actual rendering or building of the instrument is performed by a single accountable centre, which leverages AI and automation to produce survey instruments or extraction routines rapidly and at scale. Automated instrument building enables the strict enforcement of timeliness standards (such as a maximum allowed period between specification and instrument launch), with policies and procedures reformed to reflect these new practices. Direct connection of collection instruments to metadata systems is required to ensure seamless data and metadata capture at source. Staff roles and responsibilities are clearly delineated, removing ambiguity and supporting the rapid, standardized, and high-quality development of instruments for all relevant data acquisition needs.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it requires the building and reuse of collection instruments, including automated survey instruments or extraction routines, and requires that subject-matter requirements be translated into implementable specifications. This needs roles that can work with collection operations, assess system requirements, and help define how collection and processing systems should operate. The Operations Officer directly fits this need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives," and "assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems." The role also "meets with subject matter and systems specialists, clients, service providers and others, in order to comprehend and elaborate on the conditions within which statistical operations will occur," which aligns with instrument specification and build coordination.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it explicitly requires a "direct connection of collection instruments to metadata systems" and standardized, high-quality instrument development tied to metadata capture at source. This needs a role with capability in statistical metadata production, validation, requirements translation, and metadata system procedures. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills that need because the role "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository," and "liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management in order to develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata." The role also has "knowledge of survey and statistical program subject matter concepts and methodologies relevant to the collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data" and provides feedback on methods and systems for metadata production, which is directly relevant to instrument-metadata integration.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because subject matter sponsors must specify and certify collection instrument requirements, and those requirements must be translated into specifications for development under clear plans, priorities and target dates. This needs a subject-matter role able to articulate concepts, definitions, and program requirements into system specifications and propose changes to collection methods. Economist/Sociologist 2 fits this need because the role "liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development, to suggest improvements to ongoing programs, to negotiate procedural modifications and to establish project plans, priorities and target dates." It also "participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities," which directly supports specifying and refining collection instruments.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because automated instrument building includes not only survey instruments but also "extraction routines," and requires translation of subject-matter requirements into technical specifications for data capture and acquisition. This needs a role with knowledge of the data life cycle, data capture, extraction, transformation, validation, and requirements discussions with collection operations and systems specialists. The Junior Data Analyst is relevant because the role has knowledge of "data science and its life cycle, including data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing," and "conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin." The role also, "as assigned, discusses data requirements with operations managers responsible for data collection, other subject matter and systems specialists, clients or service providers to comprehend and elaborate the conditions within which statistical development and operations will occur," and "liaise[s] with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development," which aligns with building extraction-based collection instruments.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because building or reusing collection instruments requires examination of how revised processing specifications and system concepts affect data capture and integration with other systems. This needs a role that can assess impacts of new or revised specifications on data capture and processing functions and help translate user requirements into system development specifications. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer is therefore implicated because the role "liaises with other specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development and to suggest improvements to ongoing programs" and "examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems." That directly supports the coordinated development and reuse of collection instruments within broader production systems.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
description: This sub-process describes the activities to reuse existing components or build new, automation-ready components needed for the Process and Analyse phases. All components—whether dashboard modules, transformation functions, geospatial and information services, or workflow management tools—must be designed for modularity, AI/ML-driven orchestration, and seamless integration into digital, event-driven workflows. Automated self-testing, monitoring, and dynamic integration APIs are core features, enabling real-time responsiveness and automated exchange of data and instructions. Human roles focus on oversight, quality assurance, exception management, and iterative modernization of core analytic assets. The process ensures that the full analytics and processing stack evolves toward touchless, scalable, and intelligent operational pipelines.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it requires reusing or building automation-ready processing and analysis components, including transformation functions, workflow tools, modular services, and integrated processing assets for the Process and Analyse phases. That requires capability in data preparation, processing, transformation, validation, use of analytical software, and participation in project teams that support data management and analytics workflows. This work-description fills that need because it explicitly includes 'data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin' and states that the role 'supports the conduct of studies and/or projects using established quantitative statistical data analysis methods and software such as Python, SAS, STATA, R'. It also notes knowledge of the data science life cycle including 'processing' and 'modeling', which directly supports building or reusing processing and analysis components.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because automation-ready processing components must support operational processing pipelines, include testing and monitoring considerations, and integrate with existing collection, coding, and processing systems. That requires capability in statistical processing operations, system requirements assessment, testing specifications, and modification of operational systems and processes. This work-description fills that need because it states the role 'participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data', 'evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives', and 'assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems.' It also cites knowledge 'for designing the specifications for testing of applications', which aligns with the sub-process emphasis on automated self-testing and integration.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because reusable or newly built processing and analysis components must be assessed for their effect on data output, processing methods, and integration with analytical workflows, with human oversight focused on quality assurance and modernization. That requires capability to analyze current processing methods, translate subject-matter requirements into system specifications, and propose changes or alternative systems. This work-description fills that need because it says the role 'liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development' and 'analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.' It also includes participation in analysis of data and feedback on 'collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures,' which directly supports iterative modernization of analytic assets.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because processing and analysis components must integrate with downstream data products, support revised processing specifications, and maintain quality and consistency as systems evolve. That requires capability to examine operational system concepts, assess effects of revised processing specifications, and adapt outputs to new formats or definitions. This work-description fills that need because it states the role 'reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases' and 'examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems.' It also notes the role 'adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats,' which is relevant to reusable modular components and evolving processing assets.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because automation-ready processing and analysis components depend on metadata structures, documentation, and procedures that can be reused, validated, integrated, and evaluated across systems. That requires capability to participate in testing of new procedures and systems, analyze impacts of modified methods and systems, and support production and storage components that integrate into broader workflows. This work-description fills that need because it states the role 'provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata; and participates in the testing of new procedures and systems.' It also says the role 'analyzes current production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation methods, procedures and systems in order to propose enhancements or alternatives' and has 'knowledge of software used in the production, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata,' which supports modular, integration-ready component development.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Reuse or build dissemination components
description: This sub-process describes the activities to build new or reuse existing automation-ready dissemination components needed for the release of statistical products as designated in sub-process 2.1. Dissemination modules—spanning web services, open data, geospatial outputs, microdata access, and even traditional products—are built or upgraded for modularity, machine-actionability, and AI/automation-enabled production. Dynamic output generation, versioning, metadata enrichment, and seamless integration with downstream APIs are all standard, with automation ensuring real-time release, update, and consistency of all published outputs. Human staff are responsible for policy oversight, exception handling, and refinement of complex or user-specific dissemination features that automation cannot yet address.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it is specifically about building or reusing dissemination components for releasing statistical products, including automation-ready outputs, dynamic generation, metadata enrichment, and integration with downstream services. It therefore needs roles that directly support dissemination operations, adapt outputs to new formats, interpret user dissemination requirements, and contribute to system specifications for dissemination products. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the role explicitly 'edits, validates, markets and disseminates data,' 'interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations,' and 'participates on data production and dissemination teams.' The role also supports modular and evolving dissemination components through work that 'analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services' and 'adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because dissemination components are described as including 'metadata enrichment' and requiring outputs that are machine-actionable, versioned, and integrated across dissemination channels. That creates a need for roles that produce, validate, store, and disseminate statistical metadata and help translate dissemination requirements into specifications. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills that need because the role 'prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository.' It also 'provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata' and 'participates in the testing of new procedures and systems,' which aligns with building or reusing dissemination components. The role further supports integration and standardization by liaising 'to develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because automation-ready dissemination components require operational implementation, maintenance of automated processes, preparation of publication outputs, and support for system requirements tied to production and release. It therefore needs roles that work with automated operations, prepare publication-ready outputs, and assess requirements for systems supporting statistical outputs. The Operations Officer fills part of this need because the role 'participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data' and 'designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text for use in regular and ad-hoc publications.' The role also 'assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems,' which is relevant where dissemination components are being built or reused and integrated into automated production flows.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because dissemination components must support dynamic output generation, downstream integration, and refinement of user-specific dissemination features. That creates a need for roles that can translate subject-matter requirements into system specifications, analyze effects of procedural and technological changes on products and services, and support publication-oriented analytical outputs. Economist/Sociologist 2 is relevant because the role 'liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development' and 'analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services.' The role also supports publication purposes by 'participat[ing] in the analysis of statistical program data and assist[ing] in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because automation-enabled dissemination and seamless integration with downstream APIs depend on data preparation, transformation, validation, standards conformance, and translation of requirements into specifications for data development. It therefore needs roles that support the technical data lifecycle underlying dissemination components. The Junior Data Analyst is relevant because the role conducts 'data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin,' all of which support reliable automated dissemination outputs. The role also 'liaise[s] with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development' and has knowledge of the data science life cycle including 'summarization, reporting, visualization, business intelligence,' which supports dynamic and machine-actionable dissemination products.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Configure workflows
description: This sub-process configures the workflows, systems, and transformations used within all business processes—from data collection through to dissemination—to form modular, automation-ready data pipelines. Workflows are assembled, customized, and deployed using digital workflow or business process management platforms, with extensive AI/automation support for orchestration, process monitoring, and autonomous task triggering. These workflows enable seamless, hands-free movement of data and outputs between business process stages, allowing real-time responsiveness and minimizing the need for manual intervention. Human involvement is limited to oversight, rapid workflow adaptation where unique business needs arise, and exception escalation that cannot be managed automatically.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it is about configuring end-to-end workflows, systems, and transformations across collection, processing, and dissemination into automation-ready pipelines. That requires roles able to work with operational systems, data flows, processing specifications, testing requirements, and the integration of collection/coding/processing activities. The Operations Officer directly fills this need because the work includes participating in "manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," having "knowledge of systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows," and "assess[ing] and review[ing] system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems." This directly supports workflow configuration and deployment across business processes.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because configuring workflows requires translating business and subject-matter requirements into system specifications so that automated pipelines can move data and outputs between stages with minimal manual intervention. That requires a role that can connect subject-matter needs to system development and assess effects of changes in procedures and methods on outputs. Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because it "liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development," and "analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems." Those duties directly support configuring and adapting workflows.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because workflow configuration includes setting up transformations such as extraction, cleansing, transformation, validation, and other data pipeline steps so they can operate in a modular and automated way. That requires hands-on capability with the data life cycle and preparation stages that become workflow components. The Junior Data Analyst fills this need because the role "conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation," and has knowledge of "data science and its life cycle, including data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing." The role also "liaise[s] with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development," which is directly relevant to configuring workflow steps and transformations.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because configured workflows must carry data through to dissemination and therefore need integration between processing functions and downstream output systems. That requires a role that can assess how revised processing specifications affect coordination with other divisional systems and adapt outputs to new formats. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems," and "adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats." This directly supports configuring dissemination-facing workflow components within an end-to-end pipeline.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because end-to-end workflows also depend on metadata being correctly produced, stored, loaded, and disseminated within systems, and on methods and procedures being tested when workflows are configured or changed. That requires a role able to interpret requirements into specifications for metadata processes and participate in testing new procedures and systems. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management in order to develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata," "participates in the testing of new procedures and systems," and has knowledge of "methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata." This is directly relevant where workflow configuration includes metadata pipeline components and repository loading.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Test production systems
description: This sub-process is focused on testing the assembled and configured services and workflows by employing automated, AI-powered continuous testing practices. All new programs, routines, and workflow interactions are subject to automated regression and functional tests, with self-testing and monitoring embedded in all integrated components. Testing of data flows, file structure, metadata, and secure transmission is handled primarily by automated pipelines, with full audit trails and auto-generated reports to support later analysis or compliance. Human involvement is reserved for critical sign-off, investigating failed or ambiguous automated tests, managing complex escalations, and verifying regulatory or policy compliance. This approach enables faster, more reliable go-live decisions, reduces operational risk, and assures resilient deployment of production solutions.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it centers on testing assembled production services and workflows, including automated regression and functional testing, validation of data flows and file structures, and investigation of failures before go-live. This requires roles that can specify, assess, and review operational system behavior and testing requirements. The Operations Officer fills this need because the work description explicitly includes participation in automated operations and testing-related specification work: it has "knowledge of systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows, general software packages and computer languages, for designing the specifications for testing of applications, the application and conversion of databases, and the maintenance and use of databases," and it also "assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it explicitly includes testing of metadata and integrated workflow components, with automated validation and later analysis/compliance support. This requires capability to validate metadata, participate in testing new systems and procedures, and assess metadata quality impacts. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills that need because the role "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata," "participates in the testing of new procedures and systems," and has knowledge of "methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata" as well as the ability to analyze changes in those systems "to determine the need to update statistical metadata or adapt it to new formats."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because production-system testing includes checking data flows, file structures, validation outcomes, and investigating failed or ambiguous automated tests. This requires a role able to conduct data validation, assess conformity to standards, and support analysis of data-processing outputs. The Junior Data Analyst fills this need because the role "conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin," and its knowledge includes the data science life cycle covering "data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing" as well as the ability to "assess the quality of data and identify and mitigate risks to its integrity."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because testing production systems requires reviewing outputs from new or modified computer systems, validating whether processed data remain reliable, and supporting go-live decisions based on test results. This requires a role that assesses data quality from changed systems and examines revised processing specifications for integration effects. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases" and "examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because automated and integrated production-system testing must verify how changes in procedures, computer technology, and processing methods affect outputs and system behavior, especially when failures or anomalies need human investigation. This requires analytical capacity to assess impacts of procedural and technological changes on processed data and outputs. Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role "liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development" and in analysis "analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services" and "analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

title: Test statistical business process
description: This sub-process manages a field test or pilot of the statistical business process using automated orchestration and AI-driven monitoring to execute, track, and analyze pilot runs. All pilot phases—from collection instrument validation through end-to-end process testing—are tracked through digital platforms that automate data collection, process monitoring, and initial results analysis. Iterative feedback, result synthesis, and suggested improvements are generated by automated and AI-supported systems, enabling automatic identification of issues, process optimization, and faster cycling between iterations. Human experts supervise the piloting phase, make decisions regarding significant process re-designs, and provide final sign-off for transition to live operational status.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it centers on piloting and end-to-end testing of the statistical process, including collection, coding, processing, monitoring of results, and identification of operational issues before live deployment. That requires capability to implement and run collection/processing operations in test mode, evaluate methods and results, document problems, and recommend operational alternatives. The Operations Officer directly fills this need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives," and "analyses reported data and work results ... presenting findings on how the survey was conducted, problems encountered ... and recommending alternatives." The role also has knowledge used "for designing the specifications for testing of applications," which is directly relevant to pilot and process testing.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it includes automated tracking, initial results analysis, iterative feedback, and suggested improvements during pilot runs. That requires capability to prepare, cleanse, validate, and analyze pilot data using established analytical tools so that issues can be detected and evidence generated for iteration decisions. The Junior Data Analyst fills this need because the role "supports the conduct of studies and/or projects using established quantitative statistical data analysis methods and software such as Python, SAS, STATA, R," and "conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin." The role also includes knowledge of the data science life cycle including "data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing ... reporting, visualization" and knowledge to "assess the quality of data and identify and mitigate risks to its integrity," all of which are directly needed in pilot testing and AI-supported monitoring.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because pilot testing requires assessing whether collection, processing, editing, compilation, and presentation methods work as intended across the full business process, and whether procedural changes are needed before production. That requires subject-matter analysis of pilot outputs and review of methods and procedures for improvement. Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role "participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities." It also "analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems" and "assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored," which directly supports pilot evaluation and redesign decisions.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because pilot runs generate initial results that must be reviewed for validity, consistency, and the effects of new or modified systems before transition to live operations. That requires capability to assess data quality from test systems, validate outputs, and interpret implications of system changes. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases" and "edits, validates ... data." The role also "compiles data from diverse sources ... analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness" and "examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems." Those duties align directly with end-to-end pilot testing and analysis of test outputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because pilot testing includes validation of collection instruments and process documentation, and the phase depends on tracking, evaluating, and improving metadata and related procedures as systems are tested and refined. That requires capability to validate metadata, participate in testing of procedures and systems, and evaluate metadata quality impacts from process changes. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata," "provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata; and participates in the testing of new procedures and systems," and "assists with statistical metadata quality evaluations." The role also "analyzes current production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation methods, procedures and systems in order to propose enhancements or alternatives," which directly supports iterative pilot improvement.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because the pilot phase explicitly includes iterative feedback, result synthesis, and suggested improvements, all of which require structured evaluation of evidence from the test runs and synthesis of findings for decision-makers supervising the pilot. The Junior Evaluation Officer fills this need because the role "undertakes assigned tasks related to specific elements of evaluation projects such as ... identifying, gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data," "applying analytical tools and techniques to determine implications of evaluation results and formulating conclusions," and "provides input on the interpretation of data to support findings and conclusions." The role also "recommends ... enhancements to methods for retrieving data," which aligns with improving the tested business process based on pilot evidence.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

title: Finalise production systems
description: This sub-process finalises and deploys the assembled and configured processes and services—including all modified and newly-created systems—into production, utilizing automated deployment and orchestration tools to ensure readiness. Digital and AI-powered solutions generate all required documentation (technical manuals, user guides, change logs) automatically, and facilitate user onboarding and training via interactive platforms and digital learning modules. Live deployment is monitored and verified through automated tests and real-time telemetry, with issues escalated for human review only in exception cases. Manual staff activities focus on oversight, compliance validation, and approval of production readiness, ensuring the highest standards of operational efficiency and reliability.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it centres on moving configured systems into live production, verifying readiness, monitoring deployment, and approving operational use. That requires capability in operating and maintaining automated statistical operations, assessing system requirements, validating outputs, and supporting production documentation and training. The Operations Officer directly fits this need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," "prepares reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems," has knowledge "for designing the specifications for testing of applications," and "provides input to training materials concerning data collection operations and assists in training delivery." The role also supports compliance and operational oversight through knowledge of the Statistics Act and Privacy Act.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because finalising production systems includes ensuring that modified or new systems are production-ready, that outputs from those systems are valid, and that users can operate with the deployed environment. That requires capability to assess data quality from new or modified systems, understand effects of revised processing specifications, and contribute to manuals and training. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases," "examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems," and "drafts program information manuals and training packages ... and assists in the delivery of training." This aligns directly with production-readiness verification, documentation, and onboarding support.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because production finalisation explicitly includes generating required documentation, supporting user onboarding and training, and deploying systems that include metadata-related processes and services. That requires capability in metadata production systems, testing new procedures and systems, updating manuals, and ensuring policy and compliance alignment. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fits this need because the role "provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata; and participates in the testing of new procedures and systems," "provides input to documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals related to the production and dissemination of statistical metadata and assists with the delivery of training," and has knowledge of "policies, directives and guidelines directly and specifically related to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata." This supports deployment readiness, documentation, training, and compliance validation for metadata components of production systems.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because live deployment is monitored and verified through automated tests and telemetry, with human intervention focused on exception review and readiness oversight. That requires capability to assess data integrity, validate transformed and processed data, and support technical understanding of the data lifecycle in production environments. The Junior Data Analyst is relevant because the role "conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin," and has knowledge of "data science and its life cycle, including data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing... reporting, visualization, business intelligence." The role also includes assessing quality and protecting data through "data stewardship" and the ability to "protect and secure data," which supports production verification and operational reliability.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because finalising production systems requires translating subject-matter requirements into deployable system specifications, analyzing the effects of procedural and technology changes, and preparing operational documentation and training materials for production use. That requires a role that bridges subject matter and systems during implementation. Economist/Sociologist 2 fits this need because the role "liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development," "writes program information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports," and "analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services." This supports readiness assessment, documentation, and controlled transition of systems into production.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

title: Collect
description: This phase collects or gathers all necessary information (data, metadata, paradata) using digitally orchestrated, automation-enabled, and AI-supported systems. Passive data acquisition—from administrative, digital, and system-byproduct sources—is the default and preferred mode, utilizing APIs, automated feeds, and seamless system integrations wherever possible. Active, respondent-driven collection (e.g., surveys) is only used when passive sources are insufficient and must be minimized and justified. All collection methods are subject to real-time intake, validation, and traceability, with human involvement focused on exception handling, compliance oversight, and critical data quality control. The Collect phase is broken into four sub-processes (Figure 10), which can occur sequentially, in parallel, and iteratively, with automation maximizing efficiency and speed in each iteration.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The phase is implicating because it is explicitly about gathering information through collection operations, including passive acquisition, active respondent collection when necessary, real-time intake, validation, traceability, and compliance oversight.
