This requires operational capability to run and maintain collection processes, advise on collection methods, interact with respondents or data suppliers when exceptions arise, and verify data reliability and consistency. The Operations Officer directly fills this need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results," and has knowledge of "methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications." The role also supports exception handling and active collection where needed by "contact[ing] data suppliers or respondents to obtain their collaboration... [and] clarify problems or irregularities," while applying the Statistics Act and privacy requirements in collection.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The phase is implicating because Collect includes not only data but also metadata and paradata, and requires intake, validation, traceability, and system-supported collection. This creates a need to prepare, validate, store, and manage metadata that supports collection processes and ensures collected information is documented and usable across systems. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository" and has knowledge relevant to "the collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data" in order to assess metadata requirements. The role also contributes to quality and compliance through "statistical metadata quality evaluations" and awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The phase is implicating because Collect requires real-time intake, validation, traceability, and the use of automated and AI-supported systems, which means collected data must be extracted, cleansed, transformed, validated, and assessed for quality and origin. This requires technical data handling capability across the early data lifecycle. The Junior Data Analyst fills this need because the role conducts "data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin." The role's knowledge explicitly covers the data science lifecycle including "data capture and acquisition" and techniques for assessing quality, integrity, and governance of data assets, which directly supports intake validation and traceability in collection.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The phase is implicating because Collect depends on obtaining information from sources, understanding data requirements, and supporting acquisition processes, especially where active collection or source identification is needed. This requires capability to gather and acquire information from varied sources and communicate with clients and stakeholders about data requirements. The Junior Evaluation Officer is implicated because the role "provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data; gathers and acquires information and analyzes databases" and "collects diverse data and information from a variety of sources, including interviews, departmental documents... provincial and territorial governments and the Internet." The role also communicates "with clients in the data acquisition process" and identifies useful and accessible data sources, which aligns with source acquisition and collection support.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The phase is implicating because collection includes validating incoming data and ensuring collected and processed information is reliable enough for downstream use. This requires capability to assess validity of collected data, understand collection methods, and provide feedback on collection procedures. Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role "participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures" and has knowledge of "the socio-economic concepts and methods to assess the validity of collected and processed data." The role also analyzes "current collection... methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems," which supports improvement of collection operations.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The phase is implicating because Collect requires validation of incoming data and coordination between capture and processing functions in system-supported environments. This creates a need for roles that assess validity of collected data and examine how capture specifications affect downstream integration. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills part of this need because the role "edits, validates... data," "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases," and examines "new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems." Those responsibilities directly support the validation and systems-integration aspects of collection.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Create frame and select sample
description: This sub-process establishes the frame and selects the sample for this iteration of the collection, as specified in sub-process 2.4 (Design frame and sample). Automated and AI/LLM-driven technologies are employed to perform record linkage, deduplication, and harmonization across administrative, alternative, and legacy data sources, ensuring the sampling frame is accurate, comprehensive, and consistent. These tools facilitate quality assurance and enhance sample design, especially when coordinating samples between concurrent or overlapping statistical processes. Human experts review, refine, and sign off on the final sampling frame and sample selection, focusing attention on resolving any exceptions or ambiguities surfaced by automated systems.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it requires establishing a sampling frame from multiple sources, carrying out record linkage, deduplication, harmonization, and quality assurance, and then refining the resulting frame and sample. That creates a need for hands-on data preparation, cleansing, validation, assessment of data origin, and support to quantitative methods used in sampling-related work. The Junior Data Analyst directly fills this need because the role "conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin" and has knowledge of "data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing" as well as "statistical sampling."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because the frame and sample must be operationalized for collection, with attention to data sources, verification, consistency to specifications, and impacts of changes in sources and outputs on integrity and completeness. That creates a need for operational expertise in collection systems, verification methods, and assessment of source changes. The Operations Officer fills this need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," has knowledge of "methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications," and "analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because creating a frame and selecting a sample depends on understanding the survey universe, assessing the validity of source data, and proposing or refining methods when automated processes surface ambiguities or constraints. That creates a need for subject-matter and methodological analysis tied to the survey universe and collected data. The Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role has "knowledge of the subject and universe of the survey," "knowledge of the socio-economic concepts and methods to assess the validity of collected and processed data," and "analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because automated and AI/LLM-driven creation of the frame relies on integrating and validating information from administrative, alternative, and legacy sources, and on assessing consistency, reliability, and appropriateness of resulting data structures used for sample selection. That creates a need for compiling data from diverse sources and evaluating quality impacts from systems and database changes. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases" and "compiles data from diverse sources" while "analyz[ing] and evaluat[ing] data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because frame creation and sample selection must be documented consistently and aligned with statistical program concepts and methodologies, especially where automated processes harmonize multiple sources and human experts review exceptions. That creates a need for metadata support to validate definitions, standards, and consistency across programs. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata," has knowledge of "survey and statistical program subject matter concepts and methodologies relevant to the collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data," and "evaluates selected indicators of statistical metadata quality across survey and statistical programs."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Set up collection
description: This sub-process ensures that all people, processes, and technologies (e.g., apps, APIs, devices) are optimally configured to collect data and metadata, as designed, with a strong focus on automation, metadata compliance, and resource flexibility. Routine use of automation is required for recurring data acquisitions and ingestion partnerships. Minimum metadata standards must be checked and validated for every collection or acquisition, with AI-enabled tools applied to extract structured data from unstructured sources and to verify data source credibility—reducing misinformation and ensuring fitness for application. All setup activities also support a 'one workforce' model: staff are cross-trained for multiple roles and resource pools are dynamically allocated or reallocated in real time, based on AI-driven or demand-responsive input, providing greater efficiency and adaptability. For non-survey as well as survey sources, these principles support readiness, quality, and scalability by default.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it is about configuring the operational environment for collection, including people, processes, technologies, automation, and readiness for data acquisition. That requires capability in implementing and maintaining collection operations, evaluating collection procedures, configuring operational systems, and supporting training for collection staff. The Operations Officer directly fills this need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives," and "provides input to training materials concerning data collection operations and assists in training delivery." The role also supports setup of systems and workflows through "knowledge of systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows" and by preparing "reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it explicitly requires that "minimum metadata standards must be checked and validated for every collection or acquisition" and that collection technologies and processes be configured with strong metadata compliance. That requires capability to prepare, edit, validate, store, disseminate, and evaluate metadata, and to advise programs on metadata standards and procedures. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the role "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository," and "provides assistance and advice to internal clients with respect to statistical metadata, documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines." The role is also directly aligned to setup and compliance because it has knowledge of "statistical metadata concepts and frameworks," "methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata," and "analyzes changes in methods, procedures and systems ... to determine the need to update statistical metadata or adapt it to new formats."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it emphasizes automation, data ingestion, validation of acquired data and metadata, extraction of structured data from sources, and verification of source credibility and fitness for use. That requires capability in data capture and acquisition, extraction, cleansing, transformation, validation, quality assessment, and work with analytical tools that support modern automated collection environments. The Junior Data Analyst directly fills this need because the role includes "knowledge of data science and its life cycle, including data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing ... text mining, and qualitative analysis," and it "conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin." The role is also relevant to source credibility and integrity because it includes "knowledge of techniques and methods of information collection and analysis ... in order to assess the quality of data and identify and mitigate risks to its integrity" and knowledge of partnerships "to assess data provided by other levels of government for validity and integrity."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because setting up collection requires translating collection requirements into operational and system specifications, understanding the conditions under which statistical operations will occur, and assessing impacts of changes to sources, systems, and outputs on collection readiness and quality. That requires capability in operational analysis of collection and processing systems and in coordinating with subject matter, systems specialists, clients, and service providers. The Economist/Sociologist 2 fills part of this need because the role "liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development," has "knowledge of program context, program sponsors, participants and respondents to plan and organize the retrieval and processing of data," and "analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems." This makes the role directly relevant where collection setup depends on subject-matter-informed design and procedural adjustment.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because collection setup includes configuring downstream data capture and processing interfaces so that acquired data can be validated, integrated, and made fit for use at scale. That requires capability to assess effects of revised processing specifications, review data quality from systems and databases, and coordinate requirements with other specialists. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer is implicated because the role "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases," "examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems," and "liaises with other specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development." These duties support ensuring collection setup is operationally integrated and quality-assured.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because setup of collection and acquisition can include identifying useful and accessible sources, gathering information from varied sources, and supporting data acquisition processes under defined requirements. That requires capability in data research, source identification, and communication with clients and external professionals during acquisition-related activities. The Junior Evaluation Officer is implicated because the role "provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data; gathers and acquires information and analyzes databases," "identifies and recommends ... the usefulness and accessible sources of data to be used in studies," and is "required to communicate with clients in the data acquisition process." While not a primary collection-operations role, it is directly relevant to source setup and acquisition readiness aspects of this sub-process.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

title: Run collection
description: This sub-process implements data collection via a digital-first, automation-driven model, prioritizing passive, system-based, and administrative data pipelines wherever possible. Recurring external data acquisitions are orchestrated through automated scheduling and digital APIs; AI/ML tools auto-populate and validate metadata repositories and perform information management tagging as soon as data is ingested. For survey or respondent-dependent cases, AI/ML-enabled platforms optimize assignment of contacts and resources in real time—dynamically prioritizing, balancing workloads, and reallocating a single, cross-trained resource pool to improve efficiency and data quality. Manual or active contact methods are only pursued when passive collection is not feasible or complete. Continuous digital monitoring, exception reporting, and process-adjustment mechanisms further support collection quality. Human staff are primarily tasked with exception resolution, oversight, and process improvement based on analytics and feedback.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it is the operational execution of collection itself in a digital-first, automation-driven environment, including manual and automated collection, respondent follow-up when passive methods are insufficient, monitoring, exception handling, and adjustment of collection procedures. This requires capability in implementing and maintaining collection operations, advising on collection methods, resolving irregularities with data suppliers/respondents, evaluating collection results, and supporting operational improvements. The Operations Officer directly fits this need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives," and "provides assistance and advice to users on methods and practices of collection and coding." The role also explicitly supports exception resolution and respondent contact, as it "contacts data suppliers or respondents to obtain their collaboration... to clarify problems or irregularities" and prepares "monitoring procedures and management reports."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it specifies that AI/ML tools "auto-populate and validate metadata repositories" as data is ingested, making metadata production, validation, storage, and quality evaluation a direct part of running collection. This requires capability to prepare, edit, validate, and evaluate statistical metadata, support metadata repositories, and assess impacts of changed methods and systems on metadata quality. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills that need because the role "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository," and "provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata; and participates in the testing of new procedures and systems." The role also supports the quality-control aspect of collection because it "assists with statistical metadata quality evaluations" and has knowledge of "methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it depends on automated ingestion, validation, continuous digital monitoring, exception reporting, and process improvement based on analytics and feedback. That creates a direct need for data preparation, cleansing, transformation, validation, quality assessment, and analytical support to monitor collection performance and identify issues in incoming data streams. The Junior Data Analyst fills this need because the role "conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin." The role is also aligned with the digital and automated collection environment through knowledge of the data life cycle, including "data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing" and the ability to discuss requirements with "operations managers responsible for data collection."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because continuous monitoring, exception reporting, and process-adjustment mechanisms require analysis of how collection methods and procedures are performing and where improvements are needed. This creates a need for reviewing collection procedures, assessing impacts of changes, and proposing improvements to collection-related methods. Economist/Sociologist 2 is directly relevant because the role "participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities." The role also supports process-adjustment needs by "analyz[ing] current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because running collection in an automated, system-based environment still requires validation of incoming data, assessment of quality from systems and databases, and support for downstream operational use of collected data. This creates a need to review data quality from new or modified systems and to analyze consistency and reliability of collected outputs. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer is implicated because the role "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases" and "edits, validates... data." The role also supports the monitoring and exception-analysis dimension of collection because it "analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness" and "examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it includes recurring external data acquisitions, use of diverse data sources, and analytics-driven oversight and improvement of collection processes. This creates a need to gather and analyze data from multiple sources and to recommend enhancements to methods for retrieving data. The Junior Evaluation Officer is relevant because the role "provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data; gathers and acquires information and analyzes databases" and "collects diverse data and information from a variety of sources." The role also contributes to collection-method improvement because it "recommends to the Evaluation Manager, enhancements to methods for retrieving data as well as information used in the conduct of socio-economic analyses and cost-benefit analyses."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

title: Finalise collection
description: This sub-process includes loading the collected data and metadata into a suitable electronic environment for further processing, powered by AI/ML-driven validation and enrichment routines to ensure all metadata repositories and IM tagging are complete, current, and machine-actionable. Routine automatic checks identify and close metadata gaps, verify data structure and governance needs, and prepare files for downstream processing. Finalization is continuously informed by internal and external research, pilot experiments, innovation forums, and evidence-based best practices—enabling iterative improvement and world-leading quality assurance. The subject matter sponsor holds sole responsibility for certifying and accepting the finalized collection data, while operational staff focus on automation, routine execution, and surfacing improvement ideas and lessons learned. Archiving, versioning, and legal compliance handling are embedded as standard, digital-first procedures, ensuring data and metadata are always audit- and analysis-ready.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it explicitly requires loading collected data and metadata into electronic environments, validating and enriching them, ensuring repositories and tagging are complete, and preparing assets for downstream processing. That creates a direct need for a role focused on statistical metadata production, validation, repository loading, quality evaluation, and compliance. This work-description fills that need because it states that the incumbent "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository." It also directly supports metadata completeness and quality through "assists with statistical metadata quality evaluations," and supports iterative improvement because the role "provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata; and participates in the testing of new procedures and systems." The phase's emphasis on policies, governance, and legal compliance is also matched by knowledge of "policies, directives and guidelines directly and specifically related to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata" and awareness of the "Statistics and Privacy Acts."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because finalising collection requires routine execution of automated and manual operational steps to load, verify, and prepare collected files for further processing, while checking structure, completeness, and compliance. That creates a need for an operational role grounded in collection and processing workflows, verification methods, system requirements, and operational improvement. This work-description fills that need because it "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data." It is directly relevant to final checks and readiness because the role has knowledge of "methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications," and it "assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems." The phase's emphasis on surfacing lessons learned and improving procedures is also matched by the fact that the role "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives" and "analyses reported data and work results... recommending alternatives." Legal and confidentiality handling in finalisation is supported by its knowledge of the "Statistics Act" and "Privacy Acts."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it requires collected data to be loaded into an electronic environment, validated, checked for conformity and governance needs, and made analysis-ready for downstream processing. That creates a need for a role that performs data preparation, cleansing, transformation, validation, and quality assessment in a data lifecycle context. This work-description fills that need because it explicitly "conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin." It also aligns with the electronic-environment and downstream-processing aspects because the role requires knowledge of the data science life cycle, including "data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing" and data stewardship. The phase's governance and audit-readiness requirements are supported by the role's ability to advise on "governance concepts used to protect and optimize the utility of Statistics Canada’s data assets" and its knowledge of policies for "handling, tracking, filing and storing of sensitive and confidential material and information holdings, including electronic records."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because finalisation includes editing and validating collected data, reviewing quality from systems and databases, and ensuring the resulting files are ready for subsequent processing and use. That creates a need for a role directly responsible for data editing, validation, quality review, and adaptation of outputs to required formats. This work-description fills that need because it "edits, validates, markets and disseminates data" and "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases." It also supports downstream readiness because the role "examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems." The phase's requirement to ensure consistency, reliability, and readiness is further matched by the role's responsibility to "analyze and evaluate data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness" and to "adapt data to new definitions or presentation formats." Compliance expectations are also covered through knowledge of the "Statistics Act" and "Privacy Acts."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it includes iterative improvement informed by research, pilot experiments, innovation forums, and best practices, as well as assessing whether collection, processing, and editing methods remain relevant and effective. That creates a need for a role that analyzes existing methods and procedures and proposes improvements to collection and processing activities. This work-description fills that need because it "participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities." It is also relevant to assessing the effects of procedural and technological changes during finalisation because the role "analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services" and "analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems." The phase's certification context also connects to this role's understanding of validity and reliability of collected and processed data.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it explicitly says finalization is continuously informed by internal and external research, pilot experiments, innovation forums, and evidence-based best practices, and that improvement ideas and lessons learned should be surfaced. That creates a need for a role that gathers evidence, analyzes data and methods, and supports evaluation of requirements and enhancements. This work-description fills that need because it "undertakes assigned tasks related to specific elements of evaluation projects such as, conducting literature and data research, identifying, gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data" and "provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data." It also directly supports improvement of finalisation practices because it "recommends to the Evaluation Manager, enhancements to methods for retrieving data as well as information used in the conduct of socio-economic analyses and cost-benefit analyses." While not an operational finalisation role, it is directly implicated in the evidence-based improvement component of the sub-process.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

title: Process
description: This phase describes the processing of input data and their preparation for analysis, using modular, version-controlled, automation- and AI/ML-enabled digital workflows. Every sub-process—integrate, classify, check, clean, and transform input data—is configured for event-driven orchestration, reproducibility, and end-to-end automation wherever feasible, ensuring high speed, quality, and consistency. Routine manipulation, error-checking, cleaning, imputation, and integration are handled by AI-enabled modules, with 50% or more of manual interventions eliminated. All processing operations produce full audit trails and documentation for traceability, enabling rapid adjustment and continuous process improvement. Analysts and staff focus on process oversight, exception handling, and innovation, while ensuring all processed outputs are standardized, metadata-rich, and downstream-ready for analysis and dissemination. The Process phase is broken down into eight sub-processes (Figure 11), which may run sequentially, in parallel, or iteratively, as determined by automated orchestration and analytic requirements.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The phase is implicating because it is explicitly about processing input data through integration, classification, checking, cleaning, transformation, validation, standardization, and preparation for downstream analysis in automated workflows. This requires hands-on capability in data preparation, cleansing, transformation, validation, quality assessment, and use of analytical software within the data life cycle. The Junior Data Analyst directly fills this need because the work description states that the role "conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin" and has knowledge of the data science life cycle including "data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing".
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The phase is implicating because Process includes operational execution and maintenance of data coding and processing, along with verification, consistency, and adaptation of processing systems and workflows. This requires operational expertise in collection/coding/processing methods, verification of statistical data, and assessment of system requirements for processing. The Operations Officer fills this need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," has knowledge of "methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications," and "assesses and reviews system requirements" for processing systems.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The phase is implicating because Process emphasizes checking, cleaning, transforming, and preparing processed outputs so they are reliable and ready for analysis and dissemination. This requires roles that edit and validate data, assess quality from systems and databases, and examine processing specifications and integration impacts. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "edits, validates... data," "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases," and "examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions".
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The phase is implicating because Process requires outputs to be "standardized, metadata-rich, and downstream-ready for analysis and dissemination," with documentation and traceability across processing operations. This creates a need for preparing, editing, validating, storing, and evaluating statistical metadata associated with processed data and for updating metadata when methods and systems change. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata," ensures metadata is loaded to the corporate repository, and "analyzes changes in methods, procedures and systems... to determine the need to update statistical metadata or adapt it to new formats".
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The phase is implicating because Process includes oversight of processing, editing, compilation, and assessment of how processing methods affect data quality and outputs. This requires analytical capability to review processing methods and propose improvements where procedures or technologies affect results. The Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role "participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures," and "analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The phase is implicating because Process includes preparation of input data for analysis, quality checking, and synthesis of quantitative and qualitative data into usable form. This requires support for gathering, analyzing, and synthesizing data and applying analytical tools to derive usable processed inputs. The Junior Evaluation Officer is implicated because the role undertakes tasks such as "identifying, gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data" and "collects diverse data and information from a variety of sources" while applying "established methods and techniques used for sorting, summarizing, analyzing and interpreting data."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

title: Integrate data
description: This sub-process integrates data from one or more sources using automated, modular, and AI/LLM-powered pipelines. Record linkage, deduplication, and harmonization are conducted with machine learning and automation as the core methods, minimizing manual intervention. Integration pipelines are event-driven, version-controlled, and produce full audit trails for traceability and continuous improvement. Human experts intervene only to review targeted anomalies, exceptions, and complex analytic challenges, ensuring the integrated dataset is accurate, comprehensive, and ready for further analysis.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it centers on integrating data from multiple sources through automated pipelines, including data extraction, cleansing, transformation, validation, harmonization, and quality review so that the resulting dataset is accurate and ready for analysis. This requires hands-on capability in data preparation, assessing data quality, working across the data science lifecycle, and supporting data management and analysis in structured project settings. The Junior Data Analyst directly fills this need because the role "conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin" and has knowledge of the data science life cycle including "data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing" as well as "mining, clustering, modeling." The role also "participates in project teams and working groups to support data management, research and analysis," which aligns with modular integration pipelines and targeted review of anomalies.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because integrating data from one or more sources requires operational processing capability, verification of data against specifications, understanding of data flows, and assessment of how source and system changes affect integrity and completeness. The phase needs roles that can support automated and manual processing environments, evaluate methods, and help ensure reliable integrated outputs. The Operations Officer fills this need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," has knowledge of "methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications," and possesses knowledge of "systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows" for "the application and conversion of databases." The role also "analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results," which is directly relevant to integration, harmonization, and traceability.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because data integration depends on preserving and harmonizing metadata across sources so that automated pipelines can correctly interpret structures, definitions, formats, and lineage, and so that outputs remain traceable and reusable. The phase therefore needs capability in preparing, validating, storing, and evaluating metadata, as well as adapting metadata when methods and systems change. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository" and has knowledge of "methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata." The role also "analyzes changes in methods, procedures and systems used to produce, store, disseminate and evaluate the quality of statistical metadata in order to determine the need to update statistical metadata or adapt it to new formats," which directly supports harmonization, version control, and auditability in integrated pipelines.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because integrated datasets must be reviewed for consistency, reliability, appropriateness, and the effects of revised processing specifications across systems and sources. The phase needs capability to compile data from diverse sources, assess validity after processing changes, and adapt data to new definitions or formats as part of harmonization. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases" and in research and analysis "compiles data from diverse sources" and "analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness." The role also "examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems" and "adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats," which strongly matches integration, harmonization, and readiness for further analysis.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because integrating data requires assessing how collection, processing, editing, compilation, and storage conditions affect the validity of combined outputs, especially when anomalies or complex analytic issues require human review. The phase needs analytical capability to evaluate impacts of differing concepts, definitions, and procedures across sources and to propose improvements to processing methods. Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role "participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures" and has knowledge of "the socio-economic concepts and methods to assess the validity of collected and processed data, the output from computer applications, the validity of database contents and results from alternative manipulations of data." The role also "assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored" and "analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems," which is directly relevant to harmonization and exception review in integration.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because integrated data pipelines require source assessment, database analysis, and synthesis of quantitative information from multiple inputs, particularly where targeted anomalies or exceptions must be investigated by human experts. The phase needs capability to gather and analyze data from varied sources and support interpretation of integrated results. The Junior Evaluation Officer fills part of this need because the role "identif[ies], gather[s], analyz[es] and synthesiz[es] quantitative and qualitative data," "gathers and acquires information and analyzes databases," and "collects diverse data and information from a variety of sources." The role also "applies established methods and techniques used for sorting, summarizing, analyzing and interpreting data." While not as directly operational as the data-processing roles, this work-description is still implicated in the source integration and anomaly-review aspects of the sub-process.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

title: Classify and code
description: This sub-process classifies and codes input data using modular, automated, and AI/ML-powered pipelines that leverage SDMX and other international standards. Text descriptions and response data are classified and coded primarily by LLM/AI models, which assign pre-determined statistical, geospatial, or industry codes with minimal manual handling. The workflow is event-driven, digitally logged, subject to automated QA/review, and fully auditable. Manual intervention is reserved for new or ambiguous cases, or as last-resort exception handling with domain-expert validation. This approach maximizes accuracy, speed, traceability, and scalability for coding/classification at all process scales.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is directly implicating because it is specifically about coding and classification of input data, including automated pipelines, QA/review, and exception handling for ambiguous cases. It requires operational capability to run and maintain coding processes, evaluate coding methods and results, and support both manual and automated coding workflows. The Operations Officer directly fills this need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives," and has "knowledge of the concepts, methods and techniques used in the management and control of statistical collection, coding and processing activities."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because AI/ML-powered classification and coding pipelines depend on data preparation, transformation, validation, conformity to standards, and quality checks before and during automated assignment of codes. It requires technical support for preparing input data, validating outputs, and working with data science methods used in automated classification. The Junior Data Analyst fills this need because the role "conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin" and has knowledge of the data science life cycle including "processing, mining, clustering, modeling, summarization" and "text mining," all of which are directly relevant to AI/ML-based coding pipelines.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because automated classification and coding are described as leveraging "SDMX and other international standards," which creates a direct need for metadata and standards support so coded values, classifications, and structures are documented, validated, and consistently applied. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata," provides advice on "documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines," and has "knowledge of statistical metadata concepts and frameworks used within Statistics Canada, the Government of Canada and internationally" as well as knowledge of "methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because coded and classified outputs must be reviewed for validity, consistency, and integration with downstream data products, especially where automated coding is subject to QA/review and auditability requirements. It requires capability to assess processed data quality and effects of revised processing specifications. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "edits, validates, markets and disseminates data," "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases," and "examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because classification and coding, especially where manual intervention is reserved for ambiguous cases and domain-expert validation, require subject-matter assessment of concepts, definitions, classifications, and the impact of processing choices on data validity. The Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role participates in analysis and feedback on "collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures," and specifically prepares findings on "problems encountered in implementing concepts, definitions, classifications and other instructions." The role also has knowledge "to assess the validity of collected and processed data" and analyzes "current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

title: Review and validate
description: This sub-process examines and validates data using modular, automated digital tools and AI/LLM-enabled validation routines. ML and LLMs flag missing data, inconsistencies, outliers, and errors, routing only ambiguous, complex, or systemic anomalies to human experts for further investigation and correction. All validation is digitally orchestrated with complete audit logging, reproducibility, and ongoing version control. This approach ensures rapid, scalable, and transparent validation with minimal manual intervention, allowing for continuous adjustment and quality improvement.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it centers on examining and validating data, detecting missing data, inconsistencies, outliers and errors, and investigating anomalies that automated routines cannot resolve. That requires hands-on capability in data validation, data cleansing, assessing data quality, and working with analytical tools in a digital processing environment. The Junior Data Analyst directly fills this need because the role "conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin" and has knowledge of the data science life cycle including "cleansing, processing" and the ability to "assess the quality of data and identify and mitigate risks to its integrity."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because review and validation requires operational verification of statistical data, ensuring reliability and consistency to specifications, and resolving irregularities found during processing. That requires staff who work directly in collection, coding and processing operations and who can assess reported data and operational results when anomalies are detected. The Operations Officer fills this need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," has "knowledge of methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications," and "contacts data suppliers or respondents to ... clarify problems or irregularities."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it explicitly concerns validation and quality review of data, including investigation of ambiguous or systemic anomalies and ensuring transparent, reproducible validation outputs. That requires a role with direct responsibility for editing and validating data and for assessing quality impacts from systems and databases. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role explicitly "edits, validates, markets and disseminates data" and "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases." Its analytical responsibilities also include to "analyze and evaluate data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness," which directly matches review and validation.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because automated and AI-enabled validation still routes complex or systemic anomalies to human experts for further investigation and correction, and because continuous quality improvement depends on analyzing whether current processing and editing methods remain relevant. That requires subject-matter analytical capacity to assess validity of collected and processed data and to review editing and processing procedures. Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role "participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures," has knowledge of "the socio-economic concepts and methods to assess the validity of collected and processed data," and "analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it requires complete audit logging, reproducibility, version control, and transparent validation, all of which depend not only on validating data values but also on validating the metadata that documents methods, standards, and processing context. That requires capability to prepare, edit, validate and evaluate metadata quality so that validation processes remain documented and reproducible. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata," participates in "testing of new procedures and systems," and assists with "statistical metadata quality evaluations." The role also has knowledge of methods and systems used for "producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata," which supports auditability and reproducibility.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Edit and impute
description: Where data are considered incorrect, missing, unreliable, outdated, or duplicated, edits and imputations are made through automated, modular, and AI/LLM-powered digital pipelines. LLMs and ML modules suggest and apply replacements or corrections as standard, tracking all actions and metadata in a comprehensive audit trail. Human analysts intervene only for novel, complex, or systemic data problems, and for reviewing and signing off automated edits where required. This ensures fast, accurate, and transparent correction of data with minimal manual processing.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it is explicitly about correcting problematic data through editing, imputation, validation, and review of automated processing results. It requires capability in data cleansing, validation, assessing data quality, and working with processing pipelines where human analysts review exceptions and complex cases. The Junior Data Analyst directly fills this need because the role 'conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin.' The role also requires knowledge of the data science life cycle including 'cleansing, processing' and knowledge to 'assess the quality of data and identify and mitigate risks to its integrity,' which directly supports edit and impute activities in automated environments.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because edit and impute depends on detecting incorrect, missing, unreliable, outdated, or duplicated records and applying corrections while ensuring the resulting data remain valid and reliable. It requires staff who work directly on editing and validation of statistical data and who can assess outputs from processing systems. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the role explicitly 'Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data' and 'Reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases.' The work description further states that the role 'analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness,' which is central to deciding when edits or imputations are needed and whether automated corrections are acceptable.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because automated edit and imputation pipelines still require operational control over data processing, verification of results, and intervention when irregularities or systemic issues arise. It requires knowledge of processing operations, verification methods, and reliability checks on statistical data. The Operations Officer fills this need because the role 'participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data' and has knowledge of 'methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications.' The role also 'evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives,' which aligns with reviewing edit/imputation procedures and handling exceptions in processing workflows.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because edit and impute is not only a processing activity but also a methodological one: problematic data must be assessed, editing procedures reviewed, and improvements proposed when current methods are not adequate. It requires analytical capacity to assess validity of processed data and to analyze editing methods and procedures. The Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role 'participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.' The work description also notes knowledge 'to assess the validity of collected and processed data' and the ability to analyze 'current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems,' which directly supports complex or systemic edit/imputation issues.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because the phase description explicitly requires that automated edits and imputations track 'all actions and metadata in a comprehensive audit trail.' That creates a direct need for metadata preparation, editing, validation, storage, and quality evaluation so that edit/imputation actions are transparent and documented. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role 'prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository.' The role also has knowledge of methods and systems for 'producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata' and 'analyzes changes in methods, procedures and systems ... to determine the need to update statistical metadata,' which is directly relevant to maintaining metadata and auditability for automated edit and imputation pipelines.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Derive new variables and units
description: This sub-process derives data for variables and units needed to deliver required outputs using modular, automation- and AI-powered methods. Digital pipelines apply arithmetic and formula-based logic, iterating as needed and recording all derivations and transformations with a traceable audit trail. Manual intervention is reserved for rare, non-standard or complex derivations beyond automation, with staff focusing on validation and insight for exceptions. This structure maximizes efficiency, reproducibility, and transparency in all variable/unit derivation steps.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it centers on deriving new variables and units through automated and formula-based transformations, with strong needs for data transformation, processing logic, validation, and reproducible handling of derived outputs. It therefore requires a role that can perform data preparation and transformation work directly within analytical pipelines and assess resulting quality. The Junior Data Analyst fits this need because the work description explicitly includes "data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin." It also states knowledge of the data science life cycle including "processing, mining, clustering, modeling, summarization" and use of tools such as "Python, SAS, STATA, R," which directly supports modular and automated derivation of variables and units.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because deriving new variables and units depends on processing data, applying transformation rules, verifying consistency to specifications, and supporting both automated and occasional manual handling of complex derivations. It therefore requires operational capability in data processing systems and verification methods. The Operations Officer fills this need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data" and has knowledge of "methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications." The role also includes knowledge of "systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows" and work on "developing new processing systems," which is directly relevant to digital derivation pipelines and traceable transformations.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because deriving new variables and units is not only a processing activity but also requires assessing whether transformed and derived data remain valid, coherent, and suitable for output production. It therefore needs a role able to analyze processed data, assess impacts of alternative manipulations, and suggest improvements to processing and compilation methods. Economist/Sociologist 2 meets this need because the role "participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures" and has knowledge of "the socio-economic concepts and methods to assess the validity of collected and processed data, the output from computer applications, the validity of database contents and results from alternative manipulations of data." The role also "analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems," which aligns with iterative derivation and exception-focused validation.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because derived variables and units must ultimately support required outputs, which creates a need to validate transformed data, assess effects of revised processing specifications, and adapt data into usable output forms. It therefore requires a role concerned with the validity of processed data and the consequences of alternative manipulations for production outputs. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills that need because the role "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases" and has knowledge to assess "the validity of collected and processed data, the output from computer applications, the validity of database contents and results from alternative manipulations of data." The role also "adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats" and "compiles data from diverse sources" while analyzing data for "consistency, reliability and appropriateness," all of which are directly relevant when newly derived variables and units are created for downstream outputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because all derivations and transformations are to be recorded with a traceable audit trail, which creates a clear need for metadata documentation, validation, and maintenance of information about methods and transformations. It therefore requires a role that can prepare, validate, and evaluate metadata associated with derived variables and processing changes. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fits this need because the role "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository." It also has knowledge of "methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata" and "analyzes changes in methods, procedures and systems ... to determine the need to update statistical metadata or adapt it to new formats," which directly supports transparency and auditability of derivation steps.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Calculate weights
description: This sub-process creates weights for unit data records through modular, event-driven automated algorithms, according to methodologies determined in phase 2.5. All steps and formulae, including adjustments for non-response or benchmarking, are handled digitally and recorded in procedural audit logs. Staff intervene when innovative methods, unexpected results, or diagnostic reviews are needed; otherwise, the process runs hands-free, ensuring speed, precision, and traceability in weight calculation.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it requires automated statistical processing of unit-record data, application of established weighting methodologies, handling of adjustments such as non-response or benchmarking, and review of unexpected results or diagnostics. That creates a need for roles that can work with quantitative statistical methods, prepare and validate data, and support model- or method-driven processing in software environments. The Junior Data Analyst fits this need because the role "supports the conduct of studies and/or projects using established quantitative statistical data analysis methods and software such as Python, SAS, STATA, R" and "conducts data preparation techniques" including "data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality." The role also requires "knowledge of the theories, principles, practices, and methodologies of statistics and mathematics" and knowledge of "modelling," which directly supports automated weight calculation and diagnostic review.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because weight calculation is part of statistical processing and depends on reliable automated operations, verification to specifications, and assessment of processing results when anomalies arise. That creates a need for operational roles involved in automated data processing and in evaluating methods, procedures, and outputs. The Operations Officer fills that need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data" and "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives." The work description also specifies "knowledge of methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications" and the ability to "assess and review system requirements" and analyze "reported data and work results," which aligns with automated weighting execution, traceability, and intervention when unexpected results occur.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because calculating weights depends on statistical estimation concepts, methodological impacts on outputs, and analysis of processing procedures when diagnostics or unexpected results require staff intervention. That creates a need for a role with knowledge of estimation, assessment of processed data validity, and ability to analyze methodological and processing changes. Economist/Sociologist 2 fits this need because the role includes "knowledge of statistical or economic theory and principles and the relevance of their application in a computerized environment, and the methods and techniques of data gathering, statistical estimation and economic modeling." It also includes "knowledge of the socio-economic concepts and methods to assess the validity of collected and processed data" and the ability to "analyze current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems." These capabilities directly support weighting calculations and review of their effects on outputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because automated weight calculation produces processed statistical data that must be validated for consistency, reliability, and appropriateness, especially when diagnostics indicate unexpected results. That creates a need for a role that reviews processed data quality and assesses impacts of revised processing specifications and methodologies. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills that need because the role "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases" and "edits, validates" data. The work description further states that the role "analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness" and "examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions." This is directly relevant to validating outputs from automated weighting procedures.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Calculate aggregates
description: This sub-process creates aggregate data and population totals using modular, digital automation pipelines, generating all statistical summaries, weights, and dispersion measures hands-free.
