Event-driven algorithms apply the full range of aggregations, error calculations, and summary statistic logic, recording all processes in comprehensive audit logs for traceability and QA. Human expert action is required only for advanced analytic extensions or for reviewing flagged anomalies or exceptions in automated results.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it focuses on producing aggregate data, population totals, statistical summaries, weights, dispersion measures, and reviewing anomalies from automated outputs. It therefore needs capability in quantitative statistical analysis, data processing, summarization, quality assessment, and use of analytical software in a production context. The Junior Data Analyst directly fills this need because the role "supports the conduct of studies and/or projects using established quantitative statistical data analysis methods and software such as Python, SAS, STATA, R" and performs "data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality." The knowledge section also explicitly includes "processing, mining, clustering, modeling, summarization, reporting" and knowledge of "theories, principles, practices, and methodologies of statistics and mathematics," which directly supports calculation of aggregates and review of flagged exceptions.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because aggregate calculation requires transforming processed data into statistical summaries and outputs, while checking consistency, reliability, and appropriateness of results. It therefore needs a role that produces tabulations, evaluates processed data, and works with output from computer systems. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer directly matches this because the role "interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations," "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases," and in research and analysis "compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output" and "analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness." Those duties align closely with generating aggregates and validating automated summary outputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because automated aggregation depends on sound processing operations, verification against specifications, and assessment of processing results when anomalies or exceptions are flagged. It therefore needs operational expertise in statistical processing systems and in verifying reliability and consistency. The Operations Officer fills this need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives," and has knowledge of "methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications." The role also "analyses reported data and work results" and prepares findings on processing problems, which is directly relevant to reviewing exceptions in aggregate calculations.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because calculating aggregates is part of the broader statistical compilation and presentation chain, and requires assessing whether compilation methods and processed outputs remain valid and relevant. It therefore needs subject-matter analytical capacity tied to statistical estimation, compilation, and assessment of processed data. The Economist/Sociologist 2 is directly implicated because the role "participates in the analysis of statistical program data," participates in feedback on "collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures," and has knowledge of "methods and techniques of data gathering, statistical estimation" as well as "the socio-economic concepts and methods to assess the validity of collected and processed data, the output from computer applications." The role also "analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures," which supports aggregate calculation and anomaly review.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

title: Finalise data files
description: This sub-process brings together and finalizes the results of all previous sub-processes in the phase, producing data files (micro- or macro-level) in fully standardized, open, and machine-actionable formats by default. All datasets and supporting documentation are versioned, digitally logged, and immediately available for reproducible handoff to subsequent analysis or dissemination phases. Technical staff ensure compliance with standards and continuous skills development, and all processes are supported by automated documentation and audit trails, supporting immediate traceability, interoperability, and readiness for deployment across business domains.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it requires the final assembly, validation and standardization of data files for handoff to later analysis or dissemination, with emphasis on machine-actionable outputs, consistency, and readiness for deployment. That requires capability in editing, validating, adapting outputs to required formats, and assessing the effects of processing specifications on final data products. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the role "Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data," "Reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases," and "Adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats." The role also "Compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output" and "Analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness," which directly supports finalizing complete and reliable data files.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because finalised data files must be standardized, validated, traceable, and reproducible, which requires technical data preparation, cleansing, transformation, validation, maintenance of work files, and attention to standards and data origin. The Junior Data Analyst directly fills this need because the role "Conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin." The role also "Organizes and consolidates information relevant to the defined objectives of studies" and "Maintains work files," which aligns with bringing together prior outputs and supporting reproducible, logged handoff.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because finalising data files depends not only on the data values themselves but also on supporting documentation, standards compliance, interoperability, and traceability. That requires production, validation, storage and dissemination of metadata and documentation aligned with policies and standards. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the role "Prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository." The role also has knowledge of "policies, directives and guidelines directly and specifically related to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata" and "Analyzes changes in methods, procedures and systems ... to determine the need to update statistical metadata or adapt it to new formats and to determine where updates are required to existing documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals." This directly supports the sub-process requirement for supporting documentation, versioned and standardized outputs, and interoperability.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because finalising data files requires operational assurance that processed data conform to specifications, remain reliable and consistent, and are prepared within controlled processing systems that support traceability and downstream use. That requires expertise in processing operations, verification, database conversion and maintenance, and assessing impacts on output integrity. The Operations Officer fills this need because the role "Participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," has "Knowledge of methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications," and has knowledge "for designing the specifications for testing of applications, the application and conversion of databases, and the maintenance and use of databases both for regular production of statistical data and for ad hoc manipulations and retrievals." The role also "Analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results," which is directly relevant to final file readiness.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because finalised files must be suitable for subsequent analysis and dissemination, which requires assessing the validity of processed data, understanding effects of procedures and storage conditions on outputs, and proposing suitable adjustments to compilation and presentation methods. The Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role participates in analysis of statistical program data, provides feedback on "collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures," and has knowledge "to assess the validity of collected and processed data, the output from computer applications, the validity of database contents and results from alternative manipulations of data." The role also "Analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems," which supports ensuring final data files are fit, coherent and ready for downstream use.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

title: Analyse
description: In this phase, statistical outputs are produced and examined in detail using automated, AI-powered, and modular analytical pipelines. All workflows—from draft output and commentary preparation to validation and finalization—leverage digital automation and AI/ML-driven solutions, producing real-time, reproducible, and version-controlled results. Automated generation of daily write-ups, dashboards, and other standardized products is the norm, with human analysts focused on interpretation, contextualization, and providing tailored, nuanced analysis for users. Intelligent, real-time validation and anomaly detection are embedded throughout. The phase is fully iterative and feedback-driven, supporting rapid, responsive, and continuous analytic enhancement. The Analyse phase and its sub-processes are applicable to all outputs regardless of data source, and support the seamless transition to dissemination.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because it centers on producing and examining statistical outputs, validating results, generating dashboards and write-ups, and providing interpretation and contextualized analysis for users. It therefore needs roles that can conduct quantitative analysis, assess data quality, use analytical software, and communicate findings in analytical products. The Junior Data Analyst directly fills this need because the role "supports the conduct of studies and/or projects using established quantitative statistical data analysis methods and software such as Python, SAS, STATA, R" and performs "data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality." The work description also explicitly includes "reporting, visualization, business intelligence, and exploratory/ confirmatory, predictive analysis" and says writing skills are needed to develop "analytical reports, briefings and presentation material using data visualization tools," which aligns closely with automated analytical pipelines, dashboards, validation, and interpretation in Analyse.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because outputs must be analyzed in detail, trends and anomalies identified, and analytical material prepared for internal and publication purposes, with feedback loops to improve methods. It therefore needs subject-matter analytical capacity to interpret statistical series, identify developments, and assess how methods affect outputs. Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role "participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes" and "identifies statistical trends and developments." It also "participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures," matching the phase's iterative and feedback-driven analytic enhancement. Its research responsibilities include assessing "the impact and the constraints on results" and analyzing methods "to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes," which supports detailed examination and continuous improvement of outputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because it includes producing finalized statistical outputs, validating them, preparing commentary and standardized products, and supporting transition to dissemination. It therefore needs roles that compile output products, evaluate consistency and reliability, interpret user needs, and draft interpretive material. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills that need because the role "edits, validates, markets and disseminates data," "interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations," and "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases." The work description further states that the role "compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output," "summarizes and describes meaning of data," and "analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness," which directly matches output production, validation, interpretation, and preparation for dissemination in Analyse.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because it requires analytical examination of quantitative and qualitative evidence, formulation of conclusions, and preparation of supporting reporting material. It therefore needs roles able to analyze and synthesize data, apply analytical tools, interpret findings, and support reporting. The Junior Evaluation Officer is relevant because the role includes "identifying, gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data," "applying analytical tools and techniques to determine implications of evaluation results and formulating conclusions," and providing "input on the interpretation of data to support findings and conclusions." The role also provides "supporting data for sections of reports, presentations, briefing notes and memoranda," which aligns with the Analyse phase's emphasis on draft outputs, commentary preparation, and human interpretation layered onto analytical production.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because analytical outputs must be reliable, validated, and examined for consistency, and changes in outputs or systems must be assessed for their effect on program results. It therefore needs operational analytical support focused on reviewing outputs, identifying irregularities, and reporting on quality issues. The Operations Officer fills part of this need because the role "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives" and has knowledge of "methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications." Its research responsibilities include "analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results" and "analyses reported data and work results," which supports the Analyse phase's embedded validation and examination of outputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because analytical outputs moving toward dissemination require accompanying metadata that is validated, quality-assessed, and aligned with production and dissemination requirements. It therefore needs capability to validate and evaluate metadata quality so outputs remain interpretable, reproducible, and usable in downstream dissemination. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer is implicated because the role "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata" and "assists with statistical metadata quality evaluations and provides input to reports for clients and management." The role also "analyzes current production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation methods" and "evaluates selected indicators of statistical metadata quality," which supports the Analyse phase's emphasis on reproducible, version-controlled outputs and seamless transition to dissemination.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Prepare draft outputs
description: This sub-process transforms processed and finalized data into statistical outputs using automated, AI-powered pipelines. Outputs—including indices, seasonally adjusted statistics, mapped data, geo-statistical services, write-ups, dashboards, and methodological documentation—are generated by default through LLM/AI-driven automation. Human analysts intervene to interpret, refine, or tailor outputs for specialized, complex, or critical communication needs. AI-generated methodological notes and narratives accompany all outputs, documenting analytic approaches and logic. This automation-first approach maximizes efficiency, consistency, and allows analysts to focus on providing added value and insight.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it is about converting finalized data into publishable statistical outputs, including tables, dashboards, write-ups, and methodological documentation, while also requiring human refinement of automated outputs for specialized communication needs. This requires capability to compile and validate data outputs, adapt outputs into appropriate presentation formats, interpret user or program requirements, and draft explanatory material for dissemination. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the role "edits, validates, markets and disseminates data," "interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations," and "compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output" while also "summariz[ing] and describ[ing] meaning of data" and drafting "reports and articles on the interpretation and use of statistical data and the concepts, methods and techniques used."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because draft outputs include dashboards, visualizations, analytical summaries, and other AI-generated statistical products that must be reviewed, interpreted, and refined by analysts where needed. This requires capability in reporting, visualization, summarization, and use of analytical software across the data life cycle. The Junior Data Analyst fills this need because the role supports studies using statistical software and explicitly requires knowledge of the data science life cycle including "summarization, reporting, visualization, business intelligence," and has writing skills to "draft clear and simple analytical reports, briefings and presentation material using data visualization tools for managers and clients with varying levels of knowledge and understanding of data science." It also notes data literacy to "develop briefings, presentations and dashboards that contain valid and reliable data."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because preparing draft outputs includes analytical write-ups and publication-oriented material derived from processed data, and human analysts may need to interpret trends and refine outputs for internal or public use. This requires subject-matter analysis, identification of trends, and preparation of analytical material for publication purposes. The Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role "participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes," "identifies statistical trends and developments," and writes "detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology" as well as program information and management reports. These duties align directly with refining and contextualizing draft statistical outputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because outputs are required to include methodological documentation and AI-generated methodological notes and narratives accompanying statistical products. This creates a need for preparation, validation, dissemination, and quality evaluation of metadata and documentation that explain concepts, methods, and production logic. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata," ensures metadata is loaded to the corporate repository, and contributes written information to "documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals" and to "reports which describe the results of metadata quality evaluations." The role also has knowledge of metadata concepts relevant to the "collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data," which is directly relevant to methodological notes accompanying outputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because draft outputs can include statistical tables, charts, graphs, and explanatory text, and because output preparation depends on understanding how operational processing affects the quality and presentation of results. This requires capability to design output products and explain results in publication-ready forms. The Operations Officer fills this need because the role "designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text for use in regular and ad-hoc publications" and also "responds orally and in writing ... to provide information on ... the use of program results." The role further analyzes "changes to data sources and outputs" and prepares reports on survey conduct and output quality, supporting reliable draft output preparation.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because draft outputs may include reports, presentations, briefing notes, and narrative summaries derived from analyzed data, especially where human intervention is needed to interpret and communicate findings. This requires capability to synthesize quantitative and qualitative evidence and provide supporting material for report sections and presentations. The Junior Evaluation Officer fills this need because the role "identif[ies], gather[s], analyz[es] and synthesiz[es] quantitative and qualitative data," "provides input on the interpretation of data to support findings and conclusions," and "provides the Evaluation Manager with supporting data for sections of reports, presentations, briefing notes and memoranda." These activities align with preparing draft narrative outputs from finalized data, even if in an evaluation context.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

title: Validate outputs
description: This sub-process is where outputs are validated using automated, AI- and ML-powered, real-time digital workflows. Anomaly detection, benchmarking against historical data, metadata and paradata checks, macro editing, and internal/external confrontations are executed with machine-driven QA and pattern recognition. Complex, novel, or ambiguous findings are escalated to human statistics experts for review and contextual analysis, ensuring that outputs are validated rapidly, consistently, and with high assurance of quality.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it is explicitly about validating statistical outputs through anomaly detection, benchmarking, metadata checks, macro editing, and escalation of ambiguous findings for expert review. That requires capability to validate data outputs, assess consistency and reliability, review quality impacts from systems and databases, and support dissemination-ready statistical products. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the role explicitly 'Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data' and 'Reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases.' Its research and analysis duties further align with output validation: it 'Analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness' and has 'Knowledge of the socio-economic concepts and methods to assess the validity of collected and processed data, the output from computer applications, the validity of database contents and results from alternative manipulations of data.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because output validation specifically includes 'metadata and paradata checks' and machine-driven QA against standards. That requires capability to prepare, edit, validate, and evaluate metadata quality, understand metadata frameworks and policies, and assess indicators of metadata quality across programs. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the role 'Prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata' and 'assists with statistical metadata quality evaluations.' The work description also states knowledge of 'methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata' and that the role 'Evaluates selected indicators of statistical metadata quality across survey and statistical programs in accordance with pre-defined quality guidelines.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because automated validation workflows depend on data validation, anomaly identification, quality assessment, and conformity checks before outputs can be accepted or escalated. That requires capability in data preparation, cleansing, transformation, validation, and assessing data quality and integrity using analytical tools. The Junior Data Analyst fills this need because the role 'Conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin.' The knowledge section further supports this by stating the role requires knowledge of the data science life cycle including 'cleansing, processing, mining, clustering, modeling, summarization, reporting, visualization' and knowledge to 'assess the quality of data and identify and mitigate risks to its integrity.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because validating outputs includes checking reliability and consistency to specifications, confronting irregularities, and understanding whether operational or processing issues have affected final outputs. That requires capability to verify statistical data, analyze changes to outputs, and assess impacts on integrity and completeness of program results. The Operations Officer fills this need because the role includes 'Evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives' and has knowledge of 'methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications.' Its analytical responsibilities also align because it 'Analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results' and 'Analyses reported data and work results' including problems encountered and recommended alternatives.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because complex, novel, or ambiguous validation findings are escalated to human statistics experts for contextual analysis, trend interpretation, and assessment of whether outputs remain valid under different concepts, definitions, and processing conditions. That requires subject-matter analytical capability to assess validity of processed data and outputs and to analyze trends and methodological effects. The Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role 'participates in the analysis of statistical program data,' 'Identifies statistical trends and developments,' and has knowledge 'to assess the validity of collected and processed data, the output from computer applications, the validity of database contents and results from alternative manipulations of data.' The role also 'Assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored,' which is directly relevant to contextual review of ambiguous validation findings.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because some output validation activities, especially review of anomalous or ambiguous findings, require human analysis and interpretation of quantitative and qualitative evidence to support conclusions about whether outputs are credible. That requires capability to analyze and synthesize data, interpret findings, and apply analytical tools under supervision. The Junior Evaluation Officer is relevant because the role 'identif[ies], gather[s], analyz[es] and synthesiz[es] quantitative and qualitative data,' 'apply[ies] analytical tools and techniques to determine implications of evaluation results and formulat[e] conclusions,' and 'Provides input on the interpretation of data to support findings and conclusions.' While not a primary production-validation role, this work description supports the human review and interpretation aspect of escalated findings in output validation.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

title: Interpret and explain outputs
description: This sub-process interprets and explains outputs using LLM/AI-powered narrative generation, visualization, and automated analytics to provide first-draft explanations and insight. Statisticians and analysts review and refine these drafts, supplementing them with domain expertise, context, and additional analytics as needed to make results accessible and meaningful, especially for nuanced or high-impact topics.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it centers on interpreting statistical outputs, generating explanatory narratives and visualizations, and refining those explanations so results are meaningful and accessible. This requires capability in data analysis, visualization, reporting, and communicating analytical findings clearly to varied audiences. This work-description directly fits that need because it "supports the conduct of studies... using established quantitative statistical data analysis methods," has knowledge of "summarization, reporting, visualization, business intelligence," and explicitly requires writing to "draft clear and simple analytical reports, briefings and presentation material using data visualization tools for managers and clients with varying levels of knowledge and understanding of data science."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because outputs must be interpreted and explained for dissemination, often through narrative text, tables, charts, and tailored responses to user needs. This requires staff who can summarize the meaning of data, prepare explanatory products, and interpret requests in order to present results appropriately. This work-description fills that need because it "drafts reports and articles on the interpretation and use of statistical data and the concepts, methods and techniques used," and in research and analysis it "compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output" and "summarizes and describes meaning of data."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because interpreting and explaining outputs, especially for nuanced topics, requires subject-matter analysis, identification of trends, and preparation of analytical material for publication and internal use. This requires domain expertise to assess what the outputs mean and how they should be explained in context. This work-description matches that need because it "participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes," "identifies statistical trends and developments," and includes writing and presenting "subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify divisional systems and applications."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because explanatory outputs depend not only on numerical interpretation but also on clear metadata and documentation so users can understand concepts, methods, quality, and context. This requires roles that can prepare, validate, and disseminate metadata and contribute to explanatory reporting. This work-description fills that need because it "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata," provides advice to clients on metadata and standards, and "contributes written information to be used as input to reports which describe the results of metadata quality evaluations" as well as documentation that explains "policy requirements, methods, procedures and systems."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because interpretation and explanation of outputs often require understanding operational context, explaining program results, and preparing visual and textual products that communicate findings. This requires capability to design tables, charts, graphs, and explanatory text and to report on how operational factors affect outputs. This work-description supports that need because it "responds orally and in writing... to provide information on... the use of program results," "designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text for use in regular and ad-hoc publications," and "analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because interpreting and explaining outputs includes drawing implications from analyzed data and contributing supporting narrative for reports and presentations. This requires analytical synthesis, interpretation of findings, and preparation of material that helps explain results to management and stakeholders. This work-description fits that need because it undertakes "analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data," applies analytical tools "to determine implications of evaluation results and formulating conclusions," "provides input on the interpretation of data to support findings and conclusions," and provides "supporting data for sections of reports, presentations, briefing notes and memoranda."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

title: Apply disclosure control
description: This sub-process applies disclosure control by default using AI-driven, automation-enabled privacy/SCD tools, which automatically assess, suppress, or perturb outputs for confidentiality per established policy. All actions are digitally logged and audited. Outputs only reach human reviewers when the automation detects elevated, ambiguous, or non-standard disclosure risks, ensuring privacy compliance by default and at scale.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it is specifically about protecting confidentiality in outputs through automated disclosure control, applying established policy, and ensuring that only risky cases are escalated for review. This requires capability in dissemination-stage data handling, validation of outputs, and compliance with confidentiality legislation and policy. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the role "edits, validates, markets and disseminates data," "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases," and has "particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data to ensure their own actions are in compliance." The role is therefore directly implicated in applying and overseeing disclosure-controlled outputs before dissemination.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because automated disclosure control depends on operational processing systems that can assess outputs, apply suppression or perturbation rules, and maintain compliant handling of confidential data. This requires capability in automated data processing operations, verification methods, and confidentiality-aware system use. The Operations Officer fills this need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," has knowledge of "methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications," and must have "particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data to ensure their own actions are in compliance." This makes the role directly relevant to operationalizing disclosure control in automated production environments.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because AI-driven disclosure control tools must assess disclosure risk, apply confidentiality protections, and support privacy-compliant use of data assets at scale. This requires capability in data risk assessment, data preparation and validation, and responsible protection and secure use of data. The Junior Data Analyst fills this need because the role conducts "data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin," has knowledge of "data risk assessment, impact and quantitative analysis in order to assess the quality of data and identify and mitigate risks to its integrity," and includes "data stewardship" with the ability to "protect and secure data, and safeguard their responsible use." The role is therefore directly implicated in supporting automated disclosure-risk assessment and protected output preparation.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because disclosure control is applied according to established policy and must be documented, auditable, and consistently reflected in dissemination-related metadata and guidance. This requires capability in metadata validation, policy-aware documentation, and confidentiality compliance. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata," provides advice on "documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines," and has "awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of statistical information to ensure that actions are in compliance." Since disclosure control actions and restrictions need to be documented and aligned with dissemination metadata and standards, this role is directly implicated.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because outputs flagged by automation for elevated, ambiguous, or non-standard disclosure risks require human review of presentation methods, processed outputs, and compliance with confidentiality requirements. This requires capability in analyzing processed data outputs, assessing implications of methods and presentation, and applying privacy-related legislation. The Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role participates in analysis for "publication purposes," assists with feedback on "processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures," analyzes "current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems," and has "particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data." This makes the role directly relevant for review of outputs where automated disclosure control identifies non-standard risk.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

title: Finalise outputs
description: This sub-process finalises and packages outputs using digital, automation-driven tools and workflows, ensuring all required metadata, commentary, technical notes, consistency checks, and documentation are produced and collated automatically to the highest standard. Human experts are responsible for sign-off, review of flagged anomalies, and decision-making on exceptional release scenarios or nuanced dissemination requirements. Routine approval, translation, and pre-release briefing are streamlined by digital platforms, maximizing output quality and deployment speed.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it explicitly requires outputs to be finalised and packaged for dissemination, with metadata, commentary, technical notes, consistency checks, and documentation completed to a high standard. That requires a role able to edit, validate, prepare, and disseminate statistical outputs, assess output quality, adapt outputs to presentation formats, and support dissemination products. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the role "Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data," "Drafts reports and articles on the interpretation and use of statistical data," and "Compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output" while also "Analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness" and "Adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it specifically states that all required metadata must be produced and collated automatically as part of finalising outputs. That requires capability in preparing, editing, validating, storing, disseminating, and evaluating statistical metadata, as well as maintaining related documentation and quality reporting. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the role "Prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository," "Provides input to documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals related to the production and dissemination of statistical metadata," and "assists with statistical metadata quality evaluations and provides input to reports for clients and management."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because finalising outputs includes consistency checks, review of flagged anomalies, and ensuring outputs are ready for release at the highest standard. That requires analytical capability to validate data, assess quality, organize output-ready information, and support reporting products. The Junior Data Analyst is directly relevant because the role "Conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin," and also has writing capability to "draft clear and simple analytical reports, briefings and presentation material using data visualization tools." These functions support the consistency-checking and anomaly-review aspects of output finalisation.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because final output packaging includes commentary, technical notes, explanatory material, and review of output consistency before dissemination. That requires subject-matter analysis and the ability to prepare analytical material for publication purposes and assess presentation methods. Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role "participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes," and "Writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology" while also analyzing "current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures." This supports the expert review and explanatory packaging required in finalising outputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because finalisation of outputs includes technical notes, explanatory text, consistency review, and packaging of publication-ready materials. That requires operational knowledge of output preparation and the ability to prepare tables, charts, graphs, explanatory text, and reports on processing results. The Operations Officer is relevant because the role "Designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text for use in regular and ad-hoc publications," "Writes survey information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports," and has knowledge of methods "used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications." This directly supports final packaging and quality assurance of outputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it includes production of commentary, briefing material, and documentation for release, with human review and sign-off on nuanced dissemination scenarios. That requires support in preparing report sections, presentations, briefing notes, and synthesizing findings into documented outputs. The Junior Evaluation Officer is relevant because the role "Provides the Evaluation Manager with supporting data for sections of reports, presentations, briefing notes and memoranda for senior management," and "Provides input on the interpretation of data to support findings and conclusions." While not a primary dissemination role, this work-description directly aligns with the commentary and briefing components of finalising outputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

title: Disseminate
description: This phase manages the release of statistical data and their products to users using automation-driven, API-first, and metadata-enriched delivery workflows and platforms. All assembling, cataloguing, metadata enrichment, and release processes are automated and performed in real-time, producing products that are dynamically accessible, searchable, and machine-actionable by both human and AI agents. Outputs are prepared for API-driven consumption, optimized for AI search, and enriched with comprehensive metadata to ensure discovery and reuse across systems. Human staff engage only for policy setting, exception handling, and specialized user support. The Disseminate phase is structured into five sub-processes (Figure 13), which may operate sequentially, in parallel, or iteratively, as best fits the digital dissemination ecosystem.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: What makes this phase implicating is that it is explicitly about the release of statistical data and products to users, including assembling, cataloguing, metadata enrichment, searchable delivery, and specialized user support. This requires capabilities in disseminating data products, interpreting user requests, preparing outputs for publication and reuse, and supporting users. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the role explicitly 'edits, validates, markets and disseminates data,' 'interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations,' and 'provides statistical data and consultative services to users.' The role also supports dissemination outputs through 'compil[ing] data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output' and adapting 'data to new definitions or presentation formats.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: What makes this phase implicating is that dissemination in this phase is metadata-enriched, machine-actionable, searchable, and designed for discovery and reuse across systems. This requires capability to prepare, validate, store, and disseminate statistical metadata, ensure metadata quality, and support metadata standards and procedures. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the role 'prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository.' It also 'provides assistance and advice to internal clients with respect to statistical metadata, documented standards and relevant policies' and participates in 'the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata,' which aligns directly with metadata-enriched dissemination workflows.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: What makes this phase implicating is that dissemination outputs must be dynamically accessible, searchable, and usable by human and AI agents, which requires preparation of analytical outputs, presentation formats, and support to users of published information. The Economist/Sociologist 2 role is needed for analytical material and publication-oriented presentation support. This work description fits because it 'participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes,' 'provides data and assistance to users, within and outside Statistics Canada,' and has knowledge tied to the 'collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical data.' These functions support the preparation and user-facing presentation aspects of dissemination.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: What makes this phase implicating is that dissemination includes producing products that are accessible and understandable to users, often through tables, charts, graphs, explanatory text, and responses to enquiries about program results. This requires operational capability to prepare publication-style outputs and communicate results to users and the public. The Operations Officer fills part of this need because the role 'responds orally and in writing to enquiries from managers, employees and the general public to provide information on the operation of divisional systems and processes and the use of program results' and 'designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text for use in regular and ad-hoc publications.' While the role is broader operationally focused, these duties directly support dissemination products and user-facing release materials.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: What makes this phase implicating is that dissemination products in this phase must be optimized for discovery, reuse, and user consumption, which requires organizing, validating, and communicating data in reports, briefings, dashboards, and visual forms. The Junior Data Analyst is implicated because the role supports data preparation and communication products that can feed dissemination outputs. The work description states that the role conducts 'data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin' and has 'data literacy' needed to 'read, analyze, interpret, visualize and communicate data' and 'develop briefings, presentations and dashboards that contain valid and reliable data.' This supports the preparation of dissemination-ready outputs, even if the role is not a primary dissemination role.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Update output systems
description: This sub-process manages the update of output systems and databases for dissemination using automated, real-time loading of data and enriched metadata. Machine-actionable formatting, digital linkage, and metadata validation are built-in, ensuring that all disseminated products are AI- and API-consumable, searchable, and enriched with discoverability standards. Final checks for completeness and metadata enrichment are automatic, and all outputs are designed for seamless use by both human and digital consumers.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it explicitly concerns updating dissemination systems and databases with automated loading, enriched metadata, metadata validation, and discoverability-ready outputs. That requires a role able to prepare, validate, store and disseminate metadata within corporate systems, assess metadata quality, and support changes to metadata procedures and systems. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the role 'prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository,' and 'provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata; and participates in the testing of new procedures and systems.' The role also has knowledge of 'methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata' and analyzes changes 'to determine the need to update statistical metadata or adapt it to new formats,' which directly matches machine-actionable formatting, metadata enrichment, and automated validation requirements.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because dissemination outputs and databases must be updated so that data products are loaded, validated, adapted to new formats, and made available for users and digital consumers. That requires a role focused on editing, validating and disseminating data, reviewing data quality from systems and databases, and adapting outputs to revised formats and specifications. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills that need because the role 'edits, validates, markets and disseminates data,' 'reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases,' and 'participates on data production and dissemination teams.' Its analytical responsibilities include 'compil[ing] data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output,' analyzing effects of changes 'on data output, products and services,' and 'adapt[ing] data to new definitions or presentation formats,' which aligns directly with updating output systems for dissemination and ensuring outputs are consumable and complete.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because updating output systems depends on operational integration of databases, processing systems, testing specifications, and maintenance of databases used for regular production and retrieval. That requires a role with capability in automated operations, database maintenance, system requirements, and assessing impacts of changes to outputs. The Operations Officer fills this need because the role 'participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data,' and has contextual knowledge of 'systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows... for designing the specifications for testing of applications, the application and conversion of databases, and the maintenance and use of databases both for regular production of statistical data and for ad hoc manipulations and retrievals.' The role also 'analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results,' which is directly relevant to final automated checks for completeness and reliable dissemination updates.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because automated, real-time loading, validation, formatting, and AI/API-consumable dissemination require data preparation, transformation, validation, standards conformance, and support for data management workflows. That requires a role able to conduct extraction, cleansing, transformation and validation while supporting data management and governance. The Junior Data Analyst is therefore directly relevant because the role 'conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin,' and 'participates in project teams and working groups to support data management.' The knowledge base includes the data science life cycle, including 'data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing... summarization, reporting, visualization, business intelligence,' which supports the technical needs of updating dissemination systems and producing outputs suitable for digital consumption.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because updating output systems includes assessing how changes in procedures, methods, and systems affect data outputs, products, and services, and translating subject-matter requirements into system specifications for dissemination-ready outputs. That requires a role that analyzes impacts on output and presentation methods and contributes to system development specifications. The Economist/Sociologist 2 is relevant because the role 'liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development,' and in research and analysis 'analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services.' It also 'analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems,' which supports the updating of dissemination outputs and presentation formats.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

title: Produce dissemination products
description: This sub-process produces dissemination outputs using automated, AI- and LLM-powered workflows to generate, assemble, and format all products—including publications, press releases, online tables, interactive graphics, maps, and PUMFs—as standard. Text, graphics, and narrative products are created with digital automation as first resort, and all products (including mandatory PUMFs) are checked for standards adherence by human specialists, who refine outputs and ensure audience appropriateness as required. All dissemination outputs are machine-actionable, metadata-enriched, and ready for instant digital release.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it is directly about producing and disseminating statistical outputs in multiple formats, ensuring they are refined for release, and making them ready for users. That requires a role able to edit, validate, adapt, tabulate, and disseminate data products, as well as respond to user-oriented output requirements. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the role explicitly "Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data," "Interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations," and "Participates on data production and dissemination teams." Its research and analysis duties also align with assembling dissemination products, since it "Compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output," "Adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats," and drafts material "included in publications."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because dissemination outputs must be "metadata-enriched," machine-actionable, and checked for standards adherence before release. That requires a role specialized in preparing, validating, disseminating, and quality-evaluating metadata in accordance with standards and policies. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills that need because the role "Prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository," and "assists with statistical metadata quality evaluations." The work description also explicitly covers advice on "documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines" and knowledge of methods and systems for "producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata," which is central to metadata-enriched dissemination products.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it includes generating and formatting dissemination outputs such as online tables, interactive graphics, maps, and narrative products, with human refinement for audience appropriateness. That requires capability in preparing analytical reports, presentations, dashboards, visualizations, and communicating data clearly to varied audiences. The Junior Data Analyst fills this need because the role supports the data lifecycle through "summarization, reporting, visualization, business intelligence," and has writing skills to "draft clear and simple analytical reports, briefings and presentation material using data visualization tools for managers and clients with varying levels of knowledge and understanding of data science." The role also includes data preparation, validation, and conformity to standards, which supports reliable automated dissemination outputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because dissemination products include publications, explanatory text, charts, and graphs that must be assembled and formatted for release. That requires a role able to prepare publication-ready statistical visuals and explanatory content. The Operations Officer is directly relevant because the work description states that the role "Designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text for use in regular and ad-hoc publications." This is a direct match to the production of dissemination products, especially where outputs generated through automated workflows still require human checking and refinement for publication use.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because dissemination products include analytical and publication-oriented material, and human specialists must refine outputs and ensure audience appropriateness. That requires subject-matter analysis and preparation of analytical material suitable for publication. The Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role "participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes." It also "Writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify divisional systems and applications," which supports refinement of automated narrative products into audience-appropriate dissemination outputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

title: Release dissemination products
description: This sub-process releases dissemination products using digital automation to handle all elements of release—timing, briefing, embargo, subscriber access, and confidential data management. Orchestration platforms schedule, log, and manage real-time releases. Human staff review and approve exception cases, interact with high-level subscribers, and handle policy or retraction scenarios as required, ensuring transparency and compliance at all times.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it is specifically about releasing dissemination products, including managing subscriber access and confidential data management, while ensuring transparency and compliance. That requires a role with direct responsibility for disseminating statistical outputs, responding to user requests, and applying policy and confidentiality requirements during release. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the work description states that the position "Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data," "Provides statistical data and consultative services to users," and "Participates on data production and dissemination teams." It is also explicitly grounded in compliant release activity through "Knowledge of the Statistics Act ... and of Statistics Canada policies ... in the editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data" and awareness of "the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because release dissemination products includes releasing accompanying metadata and doing so through controlled dissemination processes with attention to policy, quality, and confidentiality. That requires capability to prepare, validate, and disseminate metadata that supports released products and to ensure repository and dissemination procedures are followed correctly. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills that need because the role "Prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository." The role also supports dissemination procedures and compliance through knowledge of "methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata" and explicit awareness of "the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of statistical information to ensure that actions are in compliance."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because automated release handling includes timing, subscriber access, confidential data management, and exception handling, which depend on operational systems, process controls, and communication with users and the public. That requires a role able to support automated operations, explain program results, and work within confidentiality and process requirements. The Operations Officer fills that need because the position "Participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data" and "Responds orally and in writing to enquiries from managers, employees and the general public to provide information on the operation of divisional systems and processes and the use of program results." The role is also relevant to compliant release operations because it requires "particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because release dissemination products includes briefing, interaction with high-level subscribers, and handling policy or retraction scenarios, all of which require staff who can prepare analytical material for publication and provide assistance to users. That requires subject-matter support for publication-oriented outputs and user-facing explanation of released data. Economist/Sociologist 2 fills that need because the role "participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes" and "Provides data and assistance to users, within and outside Statistics Canada." The role also supports compliant dissemination because it includes knowledge of policies and "particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because dissemination releases often require preparation of tables, charts, explanatory text, and publication-ready outputs that support the released products and associated briefings. That requires a role able to prepare publication materials and explain program results to users and the public. The Operations Officer is implicated here as well because the work description states that the position "Designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text for use in regular and ad-hoc publications" and "Responds orally and in writing to enquiries from managers, employees and the general public to provide information on the operation of divisional systems and processes and the use of program results." These duties align with the release package and communication elements of dissemination.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

title: Promote dissemination products
description: This sub-process promotes statistical products using AI/automation-driven tools to generate, recommend, and deploy messaging across all platforms—web, email, social, and beyond. Content, format, and strategy are tailored with AI for each target audience, adjusting to maximize reach and impact. Staff intervene for high-level campaign review, optimization, and the management of complex or sensitive outreach.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it is specifically about promoting dissemination products across channels and tailoring messaging, format, and strategy to audiences. That requires roles that directly support dissemination, marketing, preparation of publication-oriented content, and interaction with users and clients. This work-description fills that need most directly because it explicitly includes responsibility to "edit, validate, market and disseminate data," which aligns closely with promotion of dissemination products. It also supports outreach and explanatory content through duties to "provide statistical data and consultative services to users" and to draft "reports and articles on the interpretation and use of statistical data" for publications, which supports campaign content and audience-facing messaging.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because promotion of dissemination products depends not only on the data product itself but also on the metadata and descriptive information that help audiences discover, understand, and use the product across dissemination platforms. That requires capability in producing, validating, and disseminating metadata, as well as adapting it to methods and systems used for dissemination. This work-description fills that need because it "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata," and contributes to methods and procedures for "producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata." Its role in assisting clients and contributing to documentation and training also supports the structured descriptive content needed for promoted dissemination products.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because AI/automation-driven promotion across platforms requires analytical support for tailoring content to target audiences, preparing presentation materials, and using visualization and reporting outputs that can inform campaign optimization. That requires data analysis, reporting, visualization, and communication of findings to managers and clients. This work-description fills that need because it supports studies using analytical tools and has "data literacy" including the ability to "read, analyze, interpret, visualize and communicate data." It also explicitly supports "briefings, presentations and dashboards" and has knowledge of the data science life cycle including "reporting" and "visualization," which are relevant to AI-assisted promotion and optimization of dissemination messaging.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because promoting dissemination products requires preparation of analytical material for publication purposes and support to users inside and outside the organization, especially where messaging must reflect trends, developments, and subject-matter context. That requires capability to analyze program data, prepare publication-oriented material, and assist users. This work-description fills that need because it "participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes," identifies "statistical trends and developments," and "provides data and assistance to users, within and outside Statistics Canada." Those functions support the substantive content that promotional messaging would highlight.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because promotion across platforms often requires public-facing explanatory materials, charts, graphs, and responses to enquiries about program results. That requires capability to prepare publication content and communicate operational results to the public and stakeholders. This work-description fills that need because it "responds orally and in writing to enquiries from managers, employees and the general public to provide information on the operation of divisional systems and processes and the use of program results" and "designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text for use in regular and ad-hoc publications." While its core role is operational, these duties directly support dissemination-product promotion content and public communication.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

title: Provide user support
description: This sub-process provides user support through AI-powered chatbots and automation interfaces, which record, triage, and answer user queries in real time, guiding users to datasets, data interpretations, and publications as needed.
