Complex inquiries and escalations go to human staff for resolution, especially for nuanced, sensitive, or high-value support. User feedback and request tracking are used to populate knowledge bases and feed into service quality improvement.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it centers on answering user queries, guiding users to datasets and publications, and resolving escalated or nuanced requests that automation cannot fully handle. That requires staff who can interpret user information requests, provide consultative statistical services, and disseminate data appropriately. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the role "provides statistical data and consultative services to users," "interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations," and "edits, validates, markets and disseminates data." The role also supports explanatory user support by drafting "reports and articles on the interpretation and use of statistical data and the concepts, methods and techniques used."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because users are guided not only to datasets and publications but also to data interpretations, and complex inquiries may require human explanation of trends, concepts, and outputs. That requires staff able to assist users with statistical program data and explain analytical material. The Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role "provides data and assistance to users, within and outside Statistics Canada" and "participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes." The role also "writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology," which is directly relevant to resolving nuanced support requests.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because effective user support depends on guiding users to the right datasets, interpretations, and publications, which in turn requires accurate and accessible metadata and documentation. It also requires support content that can populate knowledge bases and help automation interfaces answer questions consistently. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata," "provides assistance and advice to internal clients with respect to statistical metadata," and contributes to "documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals." The role also analyzes and evaluates metadata quality and dissemination methods, which supports the knowledge-base and service-improvement aspects of the sub-process.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because user support includes responding to enquiries in real time and handling escalations where users need information on systems, processes, or program results. That requires staff experienced in answering enquiries and explaining operational processes clearly. The Operations Officer fills this need because the role "responds orally and in writing to enquiries from managers, employees and the general public to provide information on the operation of divisional systems and processes and the use of program results." The role also "contacts data suppliers or respondents to obtain their collaboration... [and] clarify problems or irregularities," showing capability in resolving user issues and explaining technical procedures.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because support interactions often involve helping users understand data assets, governance constraints, and appropriate use of data, especially when requests are complex or sensitive and must be escalated from automated channels. That requires staff who can advise users and clients on data use and communicate analytical information clearly. The Junior Data Analyst fills this need because the role "provides advice, information and guidance to data users and clients regarding governance concepts used to protect and optimize the utility of Statistics Canada’s data assets." The role also has the data literacy and communication capability to "read, analyze, interpret, visualize and communicate data" and to develop materials that minimize "misinterpretation," which is directly relevant to user support and interpretation guidance.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because user feedback and request tracking are used to improve service quality and populate knowledge bases, which creates a need to gather client requirements, synthesize information from interactions, and support assessment of current and future data needs. The Junior Evaluation Officer fills this need because the role "provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data," "gathers and acquires information and analyzes databases," and has communication responsibilities to "establish and maintain positive relations with Statistics Canada clients and stakeholders." The role also participates in interviews and focus groups and provides input on interpretation of data, which aligns with capturing user feedback and informing service improvement.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

title: Evaluate
description: This phase manages evaluation for each statistical business process instance using automation and AI/LLM-powered pipelines for gathering, synthesizing, and analyzing all feedback and performance metrics. Iterative, digital-first workflows continuously update and surface actionable insights, with automated reports and dashboards flagging opportunities for adjustment, learning, and quality enhancement. Human analysts focus on contextual review, recommendation adjudication, and final sign-off of improvement plans for future iterations. Evaluation may occur at the end or during any process cycle, and is broken into three sub-processes (Figure 14) which may run simultaneously or be repeated until required standards are met.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because it centers on evaluating process performance, gathering and synthesizing feedback and metrics, analyzing results, and supporting recommendations for improvement. That requires capability in formal evaluation studies, qualitative and quantitative evidence gathering, analysis, synthesis, interpretation, and reporting of findings for management review. The Junior Evaluation Officer directly fills this need because the role "participates as a member of project teams in the conduct of evaluation studies related to programs, policies and initiatives, to evaluate their relevance and performance" and "identify[ies], gather[s], analyz[es] and synthesiz[es] quantitative and qualitative data," while also "applying analytical tools and techniques to determine implications of evaluation results and formulating conclusions" and providing supporting data for "reports, presentations, briefing notes and memoranda for senior management."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because evaluation relies on gathering, preparing, validating, analyzing, and visualizing performance metrics and feedback, including automated reporting and dashboards that surface actionable insights. That requires data analysis capability across the data life cycle, including quality assessment, summarization, reporting, visualization, and support to decision-making. The Junior Data Analyst fills this need because the role "supports the conduct of studies and/or projects using established quantitative statistical data analysis methods and software," conducts "data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality," and has knowledge of the data science life cycle including "summarization, reporting, visualization, business intelligence" and the ability to "develop briefings, presentations and dashboards that contain valid and reliable data."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because evaluation includes assessing outputs, identifying trends and issues, reviewing methods and procedures, and generating feedback for future process improvement. That requires subject-matter analysis of statistical program data and the ability to assess implications of collection, processing, editing, compilation, and presentation practices. The Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role "participates in the analysis of statistical program data," "identifies statistical trends and developments," and "participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities." Its research functions also include analyzing "current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because evaluation requires reviewing data outputs and system changes for consistency, reliability, appropriateness, and impact on products and services, then communicating findings to users and managers. That requires capability in assessing data quality, interpreting results, and analyzing effects of procedural or system changes. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases," "compiles data from diverse sources," "summarizes and describes meaning of data," and "analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness." The role also "analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services," which directly supports evaluation and improvement planning.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because evaluation of a statistical business process includes reviewing operational performance in collection, coding, and processing, identifying problems encountered, and recommending alternatives for improved future iterations. That requires operational evaluation capability focused on methods, procedures, results, and reporting on implementation issues. The Operations Officer fills this need because the role explicitly "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives" and "analyses reported data and work results and prepares reports for program managers or subject matter specialists, presenting findings on how the survey was conducted, problems encountered in implementing concepts, definitions, classifications and other instructions, and recommending alternatives."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because evaluation can include assessing the quality and effectiveness of metadata that supports the statistical process, especially where automated and digital-first workflows depend on well-produced, well-evaluated metadata and documented standards. That requires capability in metadata quality evaluation, analysis of methods and systems, and reporting results for enhancement. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "assists with statistical metadata quality evaluations and provides input to reports for clients and management," "provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata," and "evaluates selected indicators of statistical metadata quality across survey and statistical programs in accordance with pre-defined quality guidelines."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Gather evaluation inputs
description: Evaluation input gathering is orchestrated via automated, AI/LLM-powered systems that harvest, aggregate, and cluster all feedback, process-metadata, quality metrics, and staff input in real time. Inputs are continuously updated and synthesized for use in ongoing and cyclical evaluation phases, easing the workload on evaluators and ensuring the highest possible input quality and completeness for downstream analysis and decision-making.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it centers on gathering and synthesizing evaluation inputs, including feedback, quality metrics, and staff input, for downstream evaluation. That requires capability to identify, gather, analyze and synthesize qualitative and quantitative information specifically for evaluation studies. The Junior Evaluation Officer directly fills this need because the role "undertakes assigned tasks related to specific elements of evaluation projects such as... identifying, gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data," and also "collects diverse data and information from a variety of sources" and participates in interviews and focus groups to obtain evaluation input.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it explicitly includes harvesting and aggregating process-metadata and quality metrics in real time. That requires capability in compiling, validating, evaluating, and reporting on statistical metadata and metadata quality. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the role "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata," "assists with statistical metadata quality evaluations," "compiles information from diverse sources in order to prepare, edit, validate and evaluate statistical metadata," and "evaluates selected indicators of statistical metadata quality across survey and statistical programs."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because the phase description emphasizes automated and AI/LLM-powered harvesting, aggregation, clustering, and continuous synthesis of inputs. That requires data lifecycle, data preparation, clustering, and quality-assessment capability to support automated input pipelines. The Junior Data Analyst directly fills this need because the role supports studies using established analytical software, "conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality," and has knowledge of the data science life cycle including "data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing, mining, clustering, modeling, summarization."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because gathering evaluation inputs includes collecting operational feedback, process results, and quality-related information from collection and processing activities. That requires operational knowledge of data collection systems, methods evaluation, and reporting on operational problems and results. The Operations Officer directly fills this need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results," and "analyses reported data and work results and prepares reports... presenting findings on how the survey was conducted, problems encountered... and recommending alternatives."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because evaluation input gathering includes assembling and analyzing statistical program data and obtaining feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods. That requires subject-matter analysis of program data and assessment of procedural impacts. The Economist/Sociologist 2 directly fills this need because the role "participates in the analysis of statistical program data," "participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures," and "analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because the phase requires aggregation of quality metrics and other inputs from data products and systems for later evaluation and decision-making. That requires compiling data from diverse sources, assessing data quality, and interpreting user or stakeholder information needs. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the role "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases," "compiles data from diverse sources," and "analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness," which directly supports assembling high-quality evaluation inputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Conduct evaluation
description: This sub-process analyzes evaluation inputs using LLM/AI-powered digital evaluation algorithms. Automated benchmarking, synthesis, and reporting produce dashboards, quality issues lists, and draft improvement recommendations for each statistical production iteration. Human experts review AI-generated outputs, contextualize findings, and finalize the recommendations and improvement plans to be carried out in current or future cycles.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it centers on analyzing evaluation inputs, synthesizing findings, producing draft recommendations, and having human experts review and finalize improvement plans. That requires evaluation-specific analytical capability, the ability to gather and synthesize qualitative and quantitative evidence, interpret findings, and support reporting and recommendations. The Junior Evaluation Officer directly fits this need because the role "participates as a member of project teams in the conduct of evaluation studies," "identify[ies], gather[s], analyz[es] and synthesiz[es] quantitative and qualitative data," "apply[ies] analytical tools and techniques to determine implications of evaluation results and formulat[e] conclusions," and "provides input on the interpretation of data to support findings and conclusions concerning various elements of evaluations." The role also supports reporting by providing "supporting data for sections of reports, presentations, briefing notes and memoranda," which aligns with evaluation reporting outputs and improvement recommendations.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because automated evaluation produces dashboards, quality issues lists, benchmarking outputs, and synthesized findings that must be analyzed and reviewed. That requires data analysis capability, preparation and validation of inputs, assessment of data quality, and production of analytical reports and dashboards. The Junior Data Analyst fills this need because the role "supports the conduct of studies and/or projects using established quantitative statistical data analysis methods and software," conducts "data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin," and has knowledge of the data science life cycle including "summarization, reporting, visualization, business intelligence" and the ability to develop "briefings, presentations and dashboards that contain valid and reliable data." These duties directly support AI-assisted evaluation analysis and dashboard/report generation.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because evaluation outputs include quality issues lists and draft improvement recommendations for statistical production iterations. That requires roles able to assess data quality, analyze consistency and reliability, summarize findings, and examine effects of procedural or system changes to support recommendations. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fits this need because the role "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases," "compiles data from diverse sources," "summarizes and describes meaning of data," and "analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness." The role also "analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services," which directly supports identifying issues and recommending improvements.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because human experts must contextualize AI-generated findings and finalize recommendations and improvement plans for statistical production cycles. That requires subject-matter analysis of program data, identification of trends and issues, and assessment of methods and procedures to support improvement recommendations. Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role "participates in the analysis of statistical program data," "identifies statistical trends and developments," and "participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities." The role also "analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems," which is directly aligned with contextualizing findings and finalizing improvements.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because evaluation of a statistical production iteration must identify operational quality issues and support recommendations for improving collection, coding, and processing operations. That requires operational analysis of methods, procedures, results, and system requirements. The Operations Officer fills this need because the role "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives," "analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results," and "analyses reported data and work results and prepares reports for program managers or subject matter specialists, presenting findings on how the survey was conducted, problems encountered ... and recommending alternatives." These responsibilities directly support quality issue identification and operational improvement planning.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because evaluation may include metadata-related quality findings and recommendations, especially where automated benchmarking and quality reporting assess the statistical production environment. That requires capability to evaluate metadata quality, analyze indicators, and contribute to reports used by management for enhancement. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fits this need because the role "assists with statistical metadata quality evaluations and provides input to reports for clients and management," "provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata," and "evaluates selected indicators of statistical metadata quality across survey and statistical programs in accordance with pre-defined quality guidelines." The role also contributes written input to reports describing "the results of metadata quality evaluations" used in enhancement of metadata management programs, which aligns with evaluation reporting and recommendations.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Agree an action plan
description: This sub-process brings together digital and AI-supported platforms for drafting, recommending, and monitoring action plans based on the synthesized evaluation. Automated dashboards and traceable tracking systems surface plan effectiveness and support human decision-makers in approving, customizing, and finalizing future improvement actions. Ongoing digital monitoring ensures that the impacts of each action feed directly into subsequent evaluation cycles, creating a robust loop of continuous improvement.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it requires action plans to be drafted and recommended from synthesized evaluation evidence, then monitored over time so that impacts feed into future evaluation cycles. That creates a need for evaluation capability: analyzing findings, determining implications, formulating conclusions, and supporting reporting to decision-makers. The Junior Evaluation Officer directly fills this need because the role "participates as a member of project teams in the conduct of evaluation studies," "identify[ies], gather[s], analyz[es] and synthesiz[es] quantitative and qualitative data," applies tools "to determine implications of evaluation results and formulat[e] conclusions," and provides "supporting data for sections of reports, presentations, briefing notes and memoranda for senior management."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it explicitly depends on digital and AI-supported platforms, automated dashboards, and traceable monitoring systems to recommend and track improvement actions. That creates a need for data preparation, analytics, dashboard production, and support for decision-use of monitored results. The Junior Data Analyst directly fills this need because the role supports studies using quantitative analysis tools, conducts "data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation," and has knowledge of the data science life cycle including "reporting, visualization, business intelligence." The work description also explicitly states that "data literacy includes data stewardship... This is needed to develop briefings, presentations and dashboards that contain valid and reliable data," which aligns closely with the automated dashboards and monitoring functions in 8.3.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because agreeing an action plan requires assessing effectiveness, reviewing evidence from current processes, and recommending future improvement actions that decision-makers can approve and customize. That creates a need for analysis of methods and procedures, identification of operational problems, and preparation of reports and recommendations. The Operations Officer directly fills this need because the role "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives," "prepares reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems," and "analyses reported data and work results... recommending alternatives." These duties align with drafting and recommending actionable improvements and supporting their operational monitoring.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because action plans are based on synthesized evaluation and must be finalized as future improvements to statistical programs and methods. That creates a need for subject-matter analysis of trends, assessment of procedural impacts, and development of recommendations for improvements. The Economist/Sociologist 2 directly fills this need because the role "participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities." The role also "analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems," which directly supports agreeing and refining an action plan.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because monitoring action-plan effectiveness and feeding impacts into subsequent evaluation cycles requires reliable outputs, interpretation of results, and assessment of how procedural or system changes affect products and services. That creates a need for data compilation, evaluation, interpretation, and adaptation of outputs for decision-makers. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the role "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases," "compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output," "summarizes and describes meaning of data," and "analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services." These capabilities support evidence-based recommendation and monitoring of improvement actions.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because traceable tracking systems and continuous improvement loops depend on clear documentation, standardized descriptions, and evaluation of information quality so that actions and their impacts can be monitored consistently over time. That creates a need for metadata production, quality evaluation, and feedback on methods and systems. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the role "provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata; and participates in the testing of new procedures and systems," "assists with statistical metadata quality evaluations," and contributes to reports used "in the enhancement of statistical metadata management programs." This supports the traceability and monitoring dimensions of the action-plan process.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
